title: 6. Measurement models per wave
text:
6.6 All constructs at a glance
How do the constructs compare? One row per construct, in two tables: its items, what was changed at T0 and the fit before and after; then how the final model holds at the eight waves of the two groups, and what Chapter 7 finds. The other tabs give the fit and the reliability of every final model at every wave in each group, and the final item sets as the later chapters read them. Models with two or three items are saturated (df = 0) and have no CFI to report (NA).

# one row per construct, group and wave, with the fitted model and whether

  select(construct, Control, Experimental) |>
  pivot_longer(-construct, names_to = "group", values_to = "fits") |>
  mutate(fits = map(fits, \(fits) tibble(wave = names(fits), fit = fits))) |>

  mutate(admissible = map_lgl(fit, \(f)
    suppressWarnings(lavInspect(f, "post.check"))))

# the lowest CFI over the eight waves, and the waves without a possible

waves_summary <- per_wave |>
  mutate(CFI = map_dbl(fit, fitMeasures, "cfi.robust")) |>
  summarise(CFI_lowest   = min(CFI[admissible]),

# items left out and residual covariances by their item numbers
glance_overview <- glance |>
  mutate(items  = map_int(full, \(f) length(lavNames(f, "ov"))),
         left_out = map2_chr(full, final, \(a, b)
           setdiff(lavNames(a, "ov"), lavNames(b, "ov")) |>
             str_extract("[0-9]+$") |>
             str_flatten_comma()),
         residuals = map_chr(final, \(f) parameterEstimates(f) |>
           filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs) |>
           transmute(pair = str_c(str_extract(lhs, "[0-9]+$"), " ~~ ",
                                  str_extract(rhs, "[0-9]+$"))) |>
           pull(pair) |>
           str_flatten_comma()),
         df        = map_dbl(final, fitMeasures, "df"),
         CFI_all   = map_dbl(full, fitMeasures, "cfi.robust"),
         CFI_final = map_dbl(final, fitMeasures, "cfi.robust")) |>
  left_join(waves_summary, by = "construct") |>
  left_join(invariance$adopted |> select(construct, chapter_7 = status),
            by = "construct") |>
  # a saturated model (df = 0) has no fit to report
  mutate(across(starts_with("CFI"), \(x) if_else(df == 0, NA, x))) |>
  transmute(construct = scales$label[match(construct, scales$scale)],
            items, `left out` = left_out, residuals,
            `CFI all` = CFI_all, `CFI final` = CFI_final,
            `lowest CFI` = CFI_lowest, `not possible` = not_possible,
            `Chapter 7` = chapter_7) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

# Measurement models of the 22 latent constructs, as Chapter 6 settles them
# at T0: the items each factor keeps and the residual covariances it needs.
# Understood has a single item and stays a manifest score.

model_items <- list(
  # Hypothesis 1: listening and togetherness
  ListenOther          = paste0("ListenOther", 1:2),
  ListenSelf           = paste0("ListenSelf", 1:2),
  KamaMuta             = paste0("KamaMuta", 1:2),
  Resonance            = paste0("Resonance", 1:8),
  Belongingness        = paste0("Belongingness", 1:3),
  NoAlienation         = paste0("NoAlienation", 1:2),
  NoIsolation          = paste0("NoIsolation", 1:2),
  # Hypothesis 2: cognitive complexity
  Rogerian             = paste0("Rogerian", c(1, 3:5)),       # 2, 6 to 9 out
  ParadoxMindset       = paste0("ParadoxMindset", 2:9),       # 1 out
  IntellectualHumility = paste0("IntellectualHumility", c(1, 3:6)), # 2 out
  ToleranceDiversity   = paste0("ToleranceDiversity", 2:5),   # 1 out
  womenAttitude        = paste0("womenAttitude", c(4, 5, 8, 9)), # 1-3, 6, 7 out
  # Hypothesis 3: well-being
  Flourishing          = paste0("Flourishing", 1:4),          # 5 to 7 out
  AutonomySatisfaction     = paste0("AutonomySatisfaction", 1:4),
  RelatednessSatisfaction  = paste0("RelatednessSatisfaction", 1:4),
  CompetenceSatisfaction   = paste0("CompetenceSatisfaction", 1:4),
  AutonomyNonFrustrated    = paste0("AutonomyNonFrustrated", 1:4),
  RelatednessNonFrustrated = paste0("RelatednessNonFrustrated", 1:4),
  CompetenceNonFrustrated  = paste0("CompetenceNonFrustrated", 1:4),
  Empowerment          = paste0("Empowerment", c(1, 3:5)),    # 2 out
  Agency               = paste0("Agency", 1:3),
  IntellectualCapital  = paste0("IntellectualCapital", 1:3)
)

# residual covariances within a wave: pairs of items with shared wording
residual_pairs <- tribble(
  ~construct,       ~item_a,           ~item_b,
  "Resonance",      "Resonance1",      "Resonance2",
  "Resonance",      "Resonance4",      "Resonance5",
  "ParadoxMindset", "ParadoxMindset4", "ParadoxMindset5",
  "ParadoxMindset", "ParadoxMindset2", "ParadoxMindset7",
  "womenAttitude",  "womenAttitude4",  "womenAttitude5",
  "Flourishing",    "Flourishing1",    "Flourishing2",
  "Empowerment",    "Empowerment4",    "Empowerment5"
)




Eight of the 22 constructs were revised at T0: they lost items, gained residual covariances, or both; the other 14 keep their items as they are. Of the 176 models at the single waves of the two groups, six are not possible, because a residual variance turns negative: Belongingness (experimental T3), Women Attitude (control T0, control T2, experimental T3), Relatedness Satisfaction (experimental T3), and Empowerment (experimental T0). Three of them fall in the experimental group’s December wave, which holds only 69 questionnaires. Among the possible models, the CFI falls below .90 in six, all in September or December: Rogerian Schema, Paradox Mindset and Tolerance Diversity. ω ranges from .49 (Agency in the experimental group at T2) to .96.
Single waves judge a model only roughly. Chapter 7 takes the four waves of each group at once, settles the models that are not possible by its stop rule, and asks whether the constructs measure the same at all four waves and in both groups.

saveRDS(list(per_wave_fit = per_wave_fit,
             per_wave_strength = per_wave_strength),
        "cache/measurement.rds")

title: 8. Simultaneous block models
text:
8.1 How each block is examined
What happens to each block? All its constructs enter one confirmatory factor model. The block goes through seven steps in three parts: its model at each wave, the block over the waves, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.





flowchart TB
  subgraph WAVE["at each wave"]
    direction LR
    S1["<b>Step 1</b><br>the model"] --> S2{{"<b>Step 2</b><br>possible? does it fit?"}}
    S2 --> S3["<b>Step 3</b><br>latent correlations"]
    S3 --> S4["<b>Step 4</b><br>discriminant validity"]
  end
  subgraph OVER["over the waves"]
    direction LR
    S5{{"<b>Step 5</b><br>adjacent waves:<br>possible? invariant?"}} --> S6{{"<b>Step 6</b><br>all four waves:<br>possible? invariant?"}}
  end
  V["<b>Step 7</b><br>what follows"]
  WAVE --> OVER
  OVER --> V
  classDef all fill:#efeff2,stroke:#8a8a8a,color:#1d1d1f
  classDef verdict fill:#ffffff,stroke:#1d1d1f,color:#1d1d1f
  class S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6 all
  class V verdict
  style WAVE fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style OVER fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a






Two rules hold along the way. At each check (the hexagons), a model whose solution is not possible stops, as in Chapter 7, and so does a model that does not fit: its latent correlations are not read, and over the waves its further levels are not taken. Unlike Chapter 7, the block models are not adjusted until they become possible. Whether the measurement of each construct stays the same over the waves and in both groups is decided in Chapter 7, construct by construct; here the block models ask whether the constructs of a block are distinct, and over the waves they check the block as a whole.
Which persons? All persons together, at each wave: discriminant validity asks whether the questionnaire separates the constructs, a property of the measures that Chapter 6 settled on both groups together; whether the groups measure alike is tested in Chapter 7.
The seven steps in detail:
At each wave:

The model. Which constructs and items the block holds, and its lavaan syntax at one wave. Each construct keeps its measurement model of Chapter 6; all factors of the block correlate freely.
The checks at each wave. The model at T0, T1, T2 and T3, fitted with robust maximum likelihood (MLR) as in Chapters 6 and 7, goes first through checks 1 to 6 of Chapter 7 (7.1, Step 3): converged, no negative variance, no correlation beyond ±1, residual covariances and latent correlations positive definite, a standard error for every parameter. A wave whose solution is not possible stops there. Then the fit: it counts as acceptable from a robust CFI of .90, the threshold the configural models of Chapter 7 have to meet, and a wave whose model does not fit stops as well. Where the model strains shows in the modification indices

of 20 or more.

The latent correlations. How closely the constructs go together at each wave whose model is possible and fits, as a heat map.
Discriminant validity. A pair of constructs counts as distinct when the upper bound of the 95 % confidence interval of its latent correlation stays below .90 (Rönkkö & Cho, 2022).

Over the waves:

Adjacent waves. Configural, metric and scalar models for the three pairs of adjacent waves (T0–T1: the experimental group trains; T1–T2: maintenance; T2–T3: the control group trains). Each model is first checked, and a window is read level by level only as long as its models are possible and pass. The configural model needs a robust CFI of at least .90, and each further level holds when the robust CFI drops by no more than .010 and the robust RMSEA rises by no more than .015 (Chen, 2007).
All four waves. The same three levels over the whole year, fitted with standard maximum likelihood, the saturated model their fit is measured against, and the same checks. Large models with many freely correlated factors and thin overlap between waves are prone to solutions at the boundary (Chen et al., 2001).

What follows:

What follows. Which verdicts stand, and where the block goes from here.

title: 8. Simultaneous block models
text:
8.2 Data and tools
Which models? Each construct keeps the items and the residual covariances of Chapter 6, now with marker identification throughout: the first item’s loading is 1, also for the two-item constructs, which the other factors of the block identify without equal loadings. Understood enters Listening and Togetherness as a factor with a single item, which carries its factor without error (residual variance 0). All factors of a block correlate freely. Over several waves, each construct has one factor per wave, and each item’s residual correlates with itself across the waves, as in Chapter 7. The metric level holds the loadings, the scalar level also the intercepts equal over the waves; at the scalar level the latent means are free from the second wave on. Two functions write the syntax, block_wave_model() for one wave and block_long_model() for several (tab Model syntax below). Two models are fitted again in this chapter, to show where their solutions break: Well-being at T2 (Step 2 of that block) and Cognitive Complexity over T0 and T1 at the metric level (Step 5 of that block).
How are they fitted? With MLR and full-information handling of missing answers, as in Chapters 6 and 7; only the four-wave models use standard maximum likelihood (Step 6). The models over several waves take hours, so all block models run in a script of their own (tab Model script). For every model it stores the fit indices (indices), the checks of its solution (checks: checks 1 to 6 of Chapter 7) and any negative variances (negative), for the models at one wave also the latent correlations (r) and the modification indices of 20 or more (mi). This chapter reads these results:

per_wave   <- readRDS("cache/block_models_wave.rds")      # 12 models
adjacent   <- readRDS("cache/block_models_adjacent.rds")  # 27 models
four_waves <- readRDS("cache/block_models_four.rds")      #  9 models
saturated  <- readRDS("cache/block_models_saturated.rds") # Step 6

Which tools? The analysis of each step is written out for every block. The functions that write the model syntax, the script that fits the models, and the functions for the checks, the decisions and the figures are shown once here:

Model syntaxModel scriptChecksDecisionsLatent correlations



# Simultaneous block models (Chapter 8): all constructs of one hypothesis
# block in one factor model, at one wave or over several waves. Marker
# identification throughout, also for the two-item constructs; Understood
# enters H1 as a single-item factor (loading 1, residual variance 0).
# Needs R/measurement.R and R/longitudinal_models.R (at(), waves).

blocks <- list(
  H1 = c("ListenOther", "ListenSelf", "Understood", "KamaMuta", "Resonance",
         "Belongingness", "NoAlienation", "NoIsolation"),
  H2 = c("Rogerian", "ParadoxMindset", "IntellectualHumility",
         "ToleranceDiversity", "womenAttitude"),
  H3 = c("Flourishing", "AutonomySatisfaction", "RelatednessSatisfaction",
         "CompetenceSatisfaction", "AutonomyNonFrustrated",
         "RelatednessNonFrustrated", "CompetenceNonFrustrated", "Empowerment",
         "Agency", "IntellectualCapital")
)
block_items <- c(model_items, list(Understood = "Understood1"))

# all items of a block, as plain names
items_of <- \(block) list_c(block_items[block])

# one wave, long data: one factor per construct, all factors correlated
block_wave_model <- \(block) {
  pairs <- residual_pairs |> filter(construct %in% block)
  c(map_chr(block, \(c)
      str_c(c, " =~ 1*", str_c(block_items[[c]], collapse = " + "))),
    if ("Understood" %in% block) "Understood1 ~~ 0*Understood1",
    str_c(pairs$item_a, " ~~ ", pairs$item_b)) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# several waves, wide data: one factor per construct and wave; metric holds
# the loadings (l_), scalar also the intercepts (t_) equal over the waves
block_long_model <- \(block, level = c("configural", "metric", "scalar"),
                      over = waves) {
  level <- match.arg(level)
  pairs <- residual_pairs |> filter(construct %in% block)

  per_construct <- map(block, \(c) {
    items <- block_items[[c]]
    labels <- if (level == "configural") rep("", length(items)) else
      str_c("l_", c, seq_along(items), "*")
    labels[1] <- "1*"
    factor <- str_c(c, "_", over)
    c(
      # loadings
      map2_chr(factor, over, \(f, w)
        str_c(f, " =~ ", str_c(labels, at(items, w), collapse = " + "))),
      # a single item carries its factor without error
      if (length(items) == 1) str_c(at(items, over), " ~~ 0*", at(items, over)),
      # intercepts (scalar) and latent means: 0, free after the first wave
      # at the scalar level
      if (level == "scalar") {
        imap(items, \(item, j) str_c(at(item, over), " ~ t_", c, j, "*1")) |>
          unlist()
      },
      str_c(factor, " ~ ", if (level == "scalar") {
        c("0*1", rep("1", length(over) - 1))
      } else {
        "0*1"
      }),
      # autocorrelated residuals of multi-item constructs
      if (length(items) > 1) {
        map(items, \(item) map_chr(combn(over, 2, simplify = FALSE), \(p)
          str_c(at(item, p[1]), " ~~ ", at(item, p[2])))) |>
          unlist()
      }
    )
  }) |>
    unlist()

  # residual covariances within each wave
  within_waves <- map2(pairs$item_a, pairs$item_b, \(a, b)
    str_c(at(a, over), " ~~ ", at(b, over))) |> unlist()

  c(per_construct, within_waves) |> str_c(collapse = "\n")
}




# Simultaneous block models of Chapter 8: per wave, over adjacent waves and
# over all four waves, for the three hypothesis blocks, and the saturated
# models behind the four-wave fit. Long: the models over several waves take
# hours. Each stage is saved as soon as it is done.
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapter 2:  Rscript scripts/block_models.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
source("R/measurement.R")
source("R/longitudinal_models.R")
source("R/block_models.R")
df      <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")      # one row per questionnaire (Chapter 2)
df_wide <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds") # one row per person (Chapter 2)

log_step <- \(...) cat(format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), ..., "\n")

# robust fit indices (MLR)
robust_fit <- \(fit) {
  fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq.scaled", "df", "cfi.robust", "rmsea.robust",
                     "srmr")) |>
    as.list() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    set_names(c("chisq", "df", "CFI", "RMSEA", "SRMR"))
}

# standard (ML) fit indices from the tests stored at fit time
standard_fit <- \(fit) {
  model    <- fit@test$standard
  baseline <- fit@baseline$test$standard
  n        <- lavInspect(fit, "ntotal")
  tibble(chisq = model$stat, df = model$df,
         CFI   = 1 - max(model$stat - model$df, 0) /
                   max(model$stat - model$df, baseline$stat - baseline$df, 0),
         RMSEA = sqrt(max(model$stat - model$df, 0) / (model$df * n)),
         SRMR  = as.numeric(fitMeasures(fit, "srmr")))
}

# convergence and admissibility, with the smallest eigenvalues of the latent
# correlations and of the residual covariances (negative: not positive
# definite), the largest correlation among the factors and among the
# residuals, and whether every free parameter has a standard error: checks
# 1 to 6 of Chapter 7 (7.1, Step 3)
admissibility <- \(fit) {
  theta <- lavInspect(fit, "theta")
  smallest_eigen <- \(m) min(eigen(m, only.values = TRUE)$values)
  correlations <- standardizedSolution(fit, se = FALSE, zstat = FALSE,
                                       pvalue = FALSE, ci = FALSE) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs)
  se <- parTable(fit) |> filter(free > 0) |> pull(se)
  tibble(converged  = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
         admissible = isTRUE(suppressWarnings(lavInspect(fit, "post.check"))),
         latent_eigen   = smallest_eigen(cov2cor(lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv"))),
         residual_eigen = smallest_eigen(theta),
         negative_residuals = sum(diag(theta) < 0),
         largest_r       = max(abs(correlations$est.std)),
         standard_errors = all(is.finite(se) & se > 0))
}

# negative variances with their z-test: a negative estimate that does not
# differ from 0 is sampling error at the boundary (Kolenikov & Bollen, 2012)
negative_variances <- \(fit) {
  parameterEstimates(fit) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs, est < 0) |>
    select(variable = lhs, est, se, z, pvalue)
}

# latent correlations with 95 % CI
latent_r <- \(fit) {
  factors <- lavNames(fit, "lv")
  standardizedSolution(fit) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs, lhs %in% factors, rhs %in% factors) |>
    transmute(pair = str_c(lhs, " ~~ ", rhs), r = est.std, ci_low = ci.lower,
              ci_high = ci.upper)
}

# 1. one wave at a time
log_step("per wave")
per_wave <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks), wave = waves) |>
  mutate(fit = map2(block, wave, \(b, w) cfa(
           block_wave_model(blocks[[b]]),
           data = df |> filter(Occasion == w) |>
             select(all_of(items_of(blocks[[b]]))),
           estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml.x")),
         indices  = map(fit, robust_fit),
         checks   = map(fit, admissibility),
         negative = map(fit, negative_variances),
         r        = map(fit, latent_r),
         mi       = map(fit, \(f) modindices(f, sort. = TRUE) |>
                              filter(mi >= 20)))
saveRDS(select(per_wave, -fit), "cache/block_models_wave.rds")

# 2. adjacent waves: T0-T1, T1-T2, T2-T3
log_step("adjacent waves")
adjacent <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks),
                        window = list(c("T0", "T1"), c("T1", "T2"),
                                      c("T2", "T3")),
                        level = c("configural", "metric", "scalar")) |>
  mutate(window = map_chr(window, \(w) str_c(w, collapse = "-")))
adjacent <- adjacent |>
  mutate(fit = pmap(list(block, window, level), \(b, w, l) {
           log_step(b, w, l)
           cfa(block_long_model(blocks[[b]], l, over = str_split_1(w, "-")),
               data = df_wide, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")
         }),
         indices  = map(fit, robust_fit),
         checks   = map(fit, admissibility),
         negative = map(fit, negative_variances))
saveRDS(select(adjacent, -fit), "cache/block_models_adjacent.rds")

# 3. the saturated model that the four-wave chi2 is measured against: does
# its EM estimate converge within the default 500 iterations, and how close
# to singular is its covariance matrix?
log_step("saturated models")
saturated_model <- \(b, iterations) {
  converged <- TRUE
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    cfa(block_long_model(blocks[[b]], "configural"), data = df_wide,
        estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml", do.fit = FALSE,
        em.h1.iter.max = iterations),
    warning = \(w) {
      if (str_detect(conditionMessage(w), "Maximum number of iterations"))
        converged <<- FALSE
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  h1 <- fit@h1  # the saturated model
  tibble(variables = length(lavNames(fit, "ov")),
         logl      = h1$logl$loglik,
         converged = converged,
         smallest_eigen = min(eigen(h1$implied$cov[[1]],
                                    only.values = TRUE)$values))
}
saturated <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks), iterations = c(500, 20000)) |>
  mutate(h1 = map2(block, iterations, saturated_model)) |>
  unnest(h1)
saveRDS(saturated, "cache/block_models_saturated.rds")

# 4. all four waves, with standard maximum likelihood (the robust
# corrections of MLR break down for models of this size) and enough EM
# iterations for the saturated model to converge (stage 3)
log_step("four waves")
four_waves <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks),
                          level = c("configural", "metric", "scalar")) |>
  mutate(fit = map2(block, level, \(b, l) {
           log_step(b, l)
           cfa(block_long_model(blocks[[b]], l), data = df_wide,
               estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml", em.h1.iter.max = 20000)
         }),
         indices  = map(fit, standard_fit),
         checks   = map(fit, admissibility),
         negative = map(fit, negative_variances))
saveRDS(select(four_waves, -fit), "cache/block_models_four.rds")
log_step("done")




# ✓ or ✗
mark <- \(x) if_else(x, "✓", "✗")

# checks 1 to 6 of Chapter 7 (7.1, Step 3), from what the script stored for
# each model: did the estimation converge, and is the solution proper? The
# tolerance for an eigenvalue at 0 is lavaan's own: a residual variance
# fixed at 0, as for Understood, sits on the boundary without crossing it
with_checks <- \(models) {
  above_0 <- \(x) x > -.Machine$double.eps^(3 / 4)
  models |>
    unnest(checks) |>
    mutate(estimation        = converged,
           variances         = map_int(negative, nrow) == 0,
           correlations      = largest_r <= 1,
           residuals         = above_0(residual_eigen),
           factors           = above_0(latent_eigen),
           `standard errors` = standard_errors,
           possible          = estimation & variances & correlations &
             residuals & factors & `standard errors`)
}

# the six checks of each model side by side, and whether it is possible
checks_table <- \(models, ...) {
  models |>
    select(..., estimation:possible) |>
    mutate(across(estimation:possible, mark))
}

# the smallest eigenvalue of the residual covariances and of the latent
# correlations of each model, against 0 (dashed): below it, the matrix is
# not positive definite and the model is not possible
plot_eigenvalues <- \(models, label) {
  models |>
    transmute(model = {{ label }},
              `residual covariances` = residual_eigen,
              `latent correlations`  = latent_eigen) |>
    pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "matrix", values_to = "eigenvalue") |>
    mutate(model  = fct_rev(fct_inorder(model)),
           matrix = fct_inorder(matrix),
           below  = eigenvalue < -.Machine$double.eps^(3 / 4)) |>
    ggplot(aes(eigenvalue, model, colour = below)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#e34948", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ matrix, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey35", `TRUE` = "#e34948"),
                        guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "smallest eigenvalue", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing.x  = unit(2, "lines"))
}




# the verdict on each model of a window, level by level: the configural
# model needs a robust CFI of at least .90, each further level a drop in
# CFI of at most .010 and a rise in RMSEA of at most .015 (Chen, 2007). A
# model is read only when every model before it in the window is possible
# and passes; the first that is not possible, does not fit or does not
# hold stops the window
step_verdicts <- \(steps) {
  steps |>
    mutate(delta_CFI   = CFI - lag(CFI),
           delta_RMSEA = RMSEA - lag(RMSEA),
           passes  = if_else(level == "configural", CFI >= .90,
                             delta_CFI >= -.010 & delta_RMSEA <= .015),
           reached = lag(cumall(possible & passes), default = TRUE),
           read    = reached & possible,
           verdict = case_when(!reached              ~ "not read",
                               !possible             ~ "not possible",
                               passes                ~ "holds",
                               level == "configural" ~ "does not fit",
                               .default = "does not hold"),
           .by = window)
}

# the fit of each model and its verdict; empty where the model is not read
fit_table <- \(steps) {
  steps |>
    mutate(across(c(chisq, df, CFI, RMSEA, delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA),
                  \(x) if_else(read, round(x, 3), NA))) |>
    select(window, level, chisq, df, CFI, RMSEA, delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA,
           verdict)
}

# the result of a window in words: the highest level that holds, and
# where the window stops
window_result <- \(level, verdict) {
  held <- level[verdict == "holds"]
  stop <- which(verdict %in% c("not possible", "does not fit",
                               "does not hold"))[1]
  if (length(held) == length(level)) return(last(held))
  stopped <- str_c(level[stop], " ", verdict[stop])
  if (length(held) == 0) stopped else str_c(last(held), "; ", stopped)
}

# the path of a block through the levels, one row per window: each tile a
# model, coloured by its verdict, with its robust CFI where it is read
verdict_colours <- c(holds = "#cdeee0", `does not fit` = "#fbdcc9",
                     `does not hold` = "#fbdcc9",
                     `not possible` = "#f6cfcf", `not read` = "#efeff2")
plot_chain <- \(steps) {
  steps |>
    mutate(level  = factor(level, levels = c("configural", "metric",
                                             "scalar")),
           window = fct_rev(fct_inorder(window)),
           label  = if_else(read, str_c(verdict, "\nCFI ", apa(CFI, 3)),
                            verdict)) |>
    ggplot(aes(level, window, fill = verdict)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3.6, lineheight = .9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = verdict_colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
}




# the latent correlations of a block as a lower triangle, one panel per
# wave: blue positive, red negative, grey near zero; framed: the pairs that
# are not distinct (upper bound of the 95 % CI at .90 or above)
plot_latent_r <- \(r, constructs) {
  labels <- set_names(scales$label, scales$scale)[constructs]
  r |>
    separate_wider_delim(pair, " ~~ ", names = c("column", "row")) |>
    mutate(row    = factor(labels[row], levels = rev(labels)),
           column = factor(labels[column], levels = labels)) |>
    ggplot(aes(column, row, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_tile(data = \(d) filter(d, ci_high >= .90), fill = NA,
              colour = "black", linewidth = .7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = apa(r)), size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ wave, ncol = 2) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#e34948", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#2a78d6",
                         limits = c(-1, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

title: 9. Means and Δd
text:
9.1 How each scale is examined
What happens to each scale? The same five steps, in the same order, for each of the 23 scales and the three hypothesis composites (Chapter 2), in three parts: the means, the effect, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.





flowchart TB
  subgraph MEANS["the means: both groups, all questionnaires"]
    direction LR
    S1["<b>Step 1</b><br>means by condition<br>and wave"]
  end
  subgraph EFFECT["the effect: both groups, the persons at both waves"]
    direction LR
    S2{{"<b>Step 2</b><br>Δd in four windows,<br>textbook conditions"}} --> S3["<b>Step 3</b><br>another standard<br>deviation"]
    S3 --> S4["<b>Step 4</b><br>multiple testing"]
  end
  V["<b>Step 5</b><br>what follows"]
  MEANS --> EFFECT
  EFFECT --> V
  classDef both fill:#f0eaf8,stroke:#8e6bbf,color:#1d1d1f
  classDef verdict fill:#ffffff,stroke:#1d1d1f,color:#1d1d1f
  class S1,S2,S3,S4 both
  class V verdict
  style MEANS fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style EFFECT fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a






The five steps in detail:
The means:

Means by condition and wave. The mean and standard deviation of the score in each group at each wave, over all questionnaires of that wave, and a figure of their course: the bars span one standard error of the mean (SD / √n) on either side, the training of the experimental group (T0 to T1) is shaded orange, that of the control group (T2 to T3) blue.

The effect:

Δd in four windows. For each group, d is the mean change from the first to the second wave of a window, divided by the standard deviation at the first wave (Morris & DeShon, 2002); change, standard deviation and standard error all rest on the persons who answered at both waves. Δd is the d of the experimental group minus the d of the control group, with a 95 % interval (Δd ± 1.96 SE) and a two-sided z-test; it counts as significant at p < .05. The four windows are the training of the experimental group (T0 to T1), its durability until September (T0 to T2) and over the full year (T0 to T3), and the training of the control group (T2 to T3), where a negative Δd means that the control group gains more. Then the textbook conditions of such a comparison, among the persons who answered at both waves: how many pairs each group has, how far apart the groups start (the difference at the first wave in pooled standard deviations, which the What Works Clearinghouse, 2020, accepts up to .25), and how many sit at the top of the scale before the window, where a gain cannot show (a ceiling effect from 15 %; Terwee et al., 2007). The conditions are reported; they change no Δd.
Another standard deviation. A common alternative divides each group’s change instead by the standard deviation of every questionnaire the group returned at the first wave of the window, whether or not the person answered again; the standard error stays that of the pairs. The question is whether a verdict (p < .05) changes.
Multiple testing. Each window tests 23 scales, so about one significant scale per window is expected by chance. The Benjamini-Hochberg correction controls the share of false discoveries among the significant results. It is applied within each window, to the 23 scales and, as a family of their own, to the three composites (one per hypothesis); an effect holds if its corrected p (pBH) stays below .05.

What follows:

What follows. Where the result goes in the later chapters, and what it amounts to as Δd.

title: 9. Means and Δd
text:
9.2 Data and tools
Which data? All questionnaires of the four waves (df, one row per questionnaire), the 26 outcomes with their readable names, and the four windows:

composites <- c("H1_ListeningTogetherness", "H2_CognitiveComplexity",
                "H3_Wellbeing")
outcomes   <- c(scales$scale, composites)

# readable names of the outcomes, the composites named by their hypothesis
outcome_labels <- c(set_names(scales$label, scales$scale),
                    H1_ListeningTogetherness = "Listening and Togetherness",
                    H2_CognitiveComplexity   = "Cognitive Complexity",
                    H3_Wellbeing             = "Well-being")

effect_windows <- tribble(
  ~pre, ~post, ~window,
  "T0", "T1",  "T0 to T1: the experimental group trains",
  "T0", "T2",  "T0 to T2: durability until September",
  "T0", "T3",  "T0 to T3: the full year",
  "T2", "T3",  "T2 to T3: the control group trains"
)

How is d computed? By two functions: d_rm() gives the change of one group in one window, delta_d() the difference between the groups for a list of outcomes, with its z-test. With sd_pre = "all" both divide by the standard deviation of Step 3. Chapters 14, 19, 21 and 22 use them again:

# Repeated-measures effect sizes (Chapters 9 and 14)
#
# d_rm(): the change of one group in one window, in standard deviations
# before the window (Morris & DeShon, 2002). Change, SD and standard error
# all come from the persons who answered at both waves.
# delta_d(): the difference experimental minus control, with a z-test.
# With sd_pre = "all", d is divided by the SD of every questionnaire of the
# group at the first wave, not only of the pairs; the standard error stays
# that of the pairs.

d_rm <- \(data, outcome, pre, post, group, sd_pre = "pairs") {
  waves <- data |>
    filter(condition == group, Occasion %in% c(pre, post)) |>
    select(id, Occasion, value = all_of(outcome))
  pairs <- waves |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Occasion, values_from = value) |>
    drop_na()
  change <- mean(pairs[[post]] - pairs[[pre]])
  d <- change / sd(pairs[[pre]])
  r <- cor(pairs[[pre]], pairs[[post]])
  n <- nrow(pairs)
  se <- sqrt(2 * (1 - r) / n + d^2 / (2 * n))
  sd_all <- sd(waves$value[waves$Occasion == pre], na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(d = if (sd_pre == "all") change / sd_all else d, se = se, n = n)
}

delta_d <- \(data, pre, post, outcomes, sd_pre = "pairs") {
  map(outcomes, \(outcome) {
    eg <- d_rm(data, outcome, pre, post, "Experimental", sd_pre)
    cg <- d_rm(data, outcome, pre, post, "Control", sd_pre)
    tibble(outcome = outcome,
           d_EG = eg$d, n_EG = eg$n, d_CG = cg$d, n_CG = cg$n,
           delta_d = eg$d - cg$d, se = sqrt(eg$se^2 + cg$se^2))
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(z = delta_d / se, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)))
}

Which tools? The two figures, the textbook conditions of Step 2 and the path at the head of each outcome use small functions, defined once here:

ConditionsPathTrajectoryEffects



# what a comparison of the two groups over one window rests on, among the
# persons who answered at both waves: the pairs of each group, how far
# apart the groups start (the difference at the first wave in pooled
# standard deviations; the What Works Clearinghouse, 2020, accepts up to
# .25), and the share of each group at the top of the scale at the first
# wave, where a gain cannot show (a ceiling effect from 15 %; Terwee et
# al., 2007)
window_conditions <- \(outcome, pre, post) {
  groups <- df |>
    filter(Occasion %in% c(pre, post)) |>
    select(id, condition, Occasion, value = all_of(outcome)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Occasion, values_from = value) |>
    drop_na() |>
    summarise(n = n(), M = mean(.data[[pre]]), SD = sd(.data[[pre]]),
              top = mean(.data[[pre]] == 10), .by = condition)
  eg <- filter(groups, condition == "Experimental")
  cg <- filter(groups, condition == "Control")
  pooled <- sqrt(((eg$n - 1) * eg$SD^2 + (cg$n - 1) * cg$SD^2) /
                   (eg$n + cg$n - 2))
  tibble(window = str_c(pre, " to ", post), n_EG = eg$n, n_CG = cg$n,
         baseline = (eg$M - cg$M) / pooled, top_EG = eg$top,
         top_CG = cg$top)
}

# the conditions of every window, ✓ where they hold
conditions_table <- \(conditions) {
  conditions |>
    transmute(window,
              pairs    = str_c(n_EG, " / ", n_CG),
              baseline = str_c(sprintf("%.2f", baseline), " ",
                               mark(abs(baseline) <= .25)),
              at_top   = str_c(round(100 * top_EG), " % / ",
                               round(100 * top_CG), " % ",
                               mark(pmax(top_EG, top_CG) <= .15)))
}

# ✓ or ✗
mark <- \(x) if_else(x, "✓", "✗")

# the windows of a set of rows, as "every window" or "the windows T0 to T2
# and T0 to T3"
windows_named <- \(windows, all) {
  if (length(windows) == all) return("every window")
  str_c(if (length(windows) == 1) "the window " else "the windows ",
        str_flatten_comma(windows, last = " and "))
}

# what the conditions say, in one or two sentences
conditions_sentence <- \(conditions) {
  apart <- conditions |> filter(abs(baseline) > .25)
  ceiling <- conditions |> filter(pmax(top_EG, top_CG) > .15)
  start <- if (nrow(apart) == 0) {
    str_c("In every window the two groups start within .25 standard ",
          "deviations of each other (at most ",
          sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(conditions$baseline))), ")")
  } else {
    str_c("In ", windows_named(apart$window, nrow(conditions)),
          " the groups start more than .25 standard deviations apart (up ",
          "to ", sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(apart$baseline))), "): there Δd ",
          "compares groups that did not start alike")
  }
  top <- if (nrow(ceiling) == 0) {
    str_c(", and at most ",
          round(100 * max(conditions$top_EG, conditions$top_CG)),
          " % of a group sits at the top of the scale before a window.")
  } else {
    str_c(". In ", windows_named(ceiling$window, nrow(conditions)),
          " more than 15 % of a group sits at the top of the scale before ",
          "the window (up to ",
          round(100 * max(ceiling$top_EG, ceiling$top_CG)),
          " %): for them a gain cannot show.")
  }
  str_c(start, top)
}




# a Δd with its p, as "0.41, p = .002"
effect_text <- \(row) {
  str_c(sprintf("%.2f", row$delta_d), ", p = ", apa(row$p, 3))
}

# the path of an outcome through the five steps, from the tables of 9.3
outcome_path <- \(name, next_text) {
  rows <- corrected |>
    filter(outcome == name) |>
    mutate(window = str_c(pre, " to ", post))
  first <- rows |> filter(pre == "T0", post == "T1")
  rest <- rows |> filter(!(pre == "T0" & post == "T1"))
  conditions <- effect_windows |>
    pmap(\(pre, post, window) window_conditions(name, pre, post)) |>
    list_rbind()
  apart <- conditions$window[abs(conditions$baseline) > .25]
  ceiling <- conditions$window[pmax(conditions$top_EG,
                                    conditions$top_CG) > .15]
  sd_rows <- sd_comparison |> filter(outcome == name)
  changed <- sd_rows |>
    filter((p < .05) != (p_all < .05)) |>
    transmute(window = str_c(pre, " to ", post))
  significant <- rows |> filter(p < .05)
  tribble(
    ~Step, ~Question, ~Result, ~Next,
    "2", "Δd while the experimental group trains (T0 to T1)?",
    str_c(effect_text(first),
          if (first$p < .05) ": significant" else ": not significant"),
    "the other windows",
    "2", "Δd in the other three windows?",
    str_flatten(str_c(rest$window, ": ", map_chr(seq_len(nrow(rest)),
                                                 \(i) effect_text(rest[i, ]))),
                "; "),
    "conditions",
    "2", "Do the groups start alike, below the ceiling?",
    c(if (length(apart) == 0) "alike in every window" else {
        str_c("more than .25 SD apart at ",
              str_flatten_comma(apart, last = " and "))
      },
      if (length(ceiling) == 0) "below the ceiling" else {
        str_c("ceiling before ", str_flatten_comma(ceiling, last = " and "))
      }) |> str_flatten("; "),
    "another SD",
    "3", "Same verdicts with the other standard deviation?",
    if (nrow(changed) == 0) "yes, in every window" else {
      str_c("no: changes at ", str_flatten_comma(changed$window,
                                                  last = " and "))
    }, "multiple testing",
    "4", "Does a significant Δd hold after the correction (BH)?",
    if (nrow(significant) == 0) "no significant Δd to correct" else {
      str_c(significant$window, ": p_BH = ", apa(significant$p_BH, 3),
            if_else(significant$p_BH < .05, ", holds", ", does not hold")) |>
        str_flatten("; ")
    }, "what follows",
    "5", "Where next?", next_text, "")
}




# the means of both groups at the four waves, with one standard error on
# either side; the two training periods shaded in the colour of the group
plot_trajectory <- \(means) {
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = .3)     # the two groups side by side
  means |>
    mutate(se = SD / sqrt(n)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = Occasion, y = M, colour = condition, shape = condition,
               group = condition)) +
    scale_x_discrete() +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 1, xmax = 2, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#eb6834", alpha = .08) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 3, xmax = 4, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .08) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = M - se, ymax = M + se), linewidth = .5,
                   position = dodge) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .7, position = dodge) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, position = dodge) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Control = "#2a78d6",
                                   Experimental = "#eb6834")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean (0 to 10)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}




# Δd with its 95 % interval, one panel per hypothesis block and window;
# filled points are significant (p < .05), open points are not
plot_effects <- \(effects) {
  effects |>
    mutate(block   = coalesce(scales$block[match(outcome, scales$scale)],
                              "Composites") |>
                       factor(levels = c("H1", "H2", "H3", "Composites")),
           outcome = factor(outcome_labels[outcome],
                            levels = rev(outcome_labels[outcomes])),
           window  = str_replace(window, ": ", "\n"),
           ci_low  = delta_d - qnorm(.975) * se,
           ci_high = delta_d + qnorm(.975) * se,
           test    = if_else(p < .05, "p < .05", "p ≥ .05")) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = delta_d, y = outcome, xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high,
               colour = test, fill = test)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_linerange(linewidth = .5) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.2, stroke = .6) +
    facet_grid(block ~ window, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("p < .05" = "grey15",
                                   "p ≥ .05" = "grey55")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("p < .05" = "grey15",
                                 "p ≥ .05" = "white")) +
    labs(x = "Δd, experimental minus control, with 95 % interval",
         y = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = .2))
}

title: 9. Means and Δd
section: 9.3 Means and Δd of all outcomes
text:
9.3 Means and Δd of all outcomes
What do the steps rest on? Four tables, computed here once for all 26 outcomes, since Step 4 compares the scales of a window with each other and the table at the end sets all outcomes side by side. Each scale section below takes its rows from them. First the means of every outcome in every group and wave (Step 1):

means_by_cell <- df |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(outcomes), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") |>
  summarise(M  = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            n  = sum(!is.na(value)),
            .by = c(outcome, condition, Occasion))

Then the d of both groups and Δd in the four windows (Step 2):

effects <- effect_windows |>
  mutate(table = map2(pre, post, \(a, b) delta_d(df, a, b, outcomes))) |>
  unnest(table)

How many persons does each window rest on?

effects |>
  filter(outcome == "H1_ListeningTogetherness") |>
  select(window, n_EG, n_CG)

The experimental group’s pairs shrink from 148 (T0 to T1) to 66 (T0 to T3), so the later windows describe ever more selected persons. The multilevel models of Chapter 10 use all questionnaires; Section 9.8 asks whether the selection explains the later gains.
The same with the standard deviation of all questionnaires before the window, and both side by side (Step 3):

effects_all_sd <- effect_windows |>
  mutate(table = map2(pre, post, \(a, b) delta_d(df, a, b, outcomes,
                                                 sd_pre = "all"))) |>
  unnest(table)

# both definitions side by side
sd_comparison <- effects |>
  select(pre, post, window, outcome, delta_d, p) |>
  left_join(effects_all_sd |>
              select(window, outcome, delta_d_all = delta_d, p_all = p),
            by = c("window", "outcome"))

And the p corrected within each window, with the 23 scales and the three composites as two families (Step 4):

corrected <- effects |>
  mutate(family = if_else(outcome %in% scales$scale, "scales",
                          "composites")) |>
  mutate(p_BH = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(window, family))

The two standard deviations differ by at most 0.11 units of Δd. While the experimental group trains, every scale keeps its verdict: the 9 in favour of the training and No Alienation against it. While the control group trains, 9 become 5: Kama Muta, Positivity Resonance, Women Attitude, and Flourishing miss significance, as their Δd shrinks (p from .050 to .093). Empowerment and Competence Non-Frustrated lose it from T0 to T2 and from T0 to T3, respectively. No verdict turns the other way, and the composites keep theirs in every window.
The correction leaves little of the scale effects: of the 10 scales significant while the experimental group trains (No Alienation against the training included), only Paradox Mindset holds (pBH < .001); the other 9 sit just above the threshold (pBH from .052 to .067). No scale effect in the other three windows survives. The composites do: Cognitive Complexity while the experimental group trains, and Listening and Togetherness and Cognitive Complexity while the control group trains, stay significant among the three hypotheses. Single scale effects of Δd should therefore be read as a pattern, not one by one. Section 10.7 applies the same correction to the multilevel models.
How large and how precise is each effect? Δd with its 95 % interval (Δd ± 1.96 SE), by hypothesis block and window. Filled points are significant (p < .05), open points are not:

plot_effects(effects)








The intervals are wide: their median width grows from 0.44 units of Δd while the experimental group trains to 0.68 over the full year, as the pairs thin out. Single scales are therefore estimated loosely; the pattern across scales and windows carries more weight than any one interval. Chapter 10 tests the same contrasts with all questionnaires, in the preregistered multilevel models.

title: 10. Multilevel models
text:
10.1 How each outcome is examined
What happens to each outcome? The outcomes are the 23 scale scores and the three hypothesis composites (Chapter 2). Each goes through the same eight steps, in the same order and in four parts: the model, the effects, their robustness, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.





flowchart TB
  subgraph MODEL["the model"]
    direction LR
    S1{{"<b>Step 1</b><br>the model and<br>its checks"}} --> S2["<b>Step 2</b><br>the random<br>structure"]
  end
  subgraph EFFECTS["the effects"]
    direction LR
    S3["<b>Step 3</b><br>the interactions"] --> S4["<b>Step 4</b><br>one-sided tests"]
    S4 --> S5["<b>Step 5</b><br>the replication"]
  end
  subgraph ROBUST["robustness"]
    direction LR
    S6["<b>Step 6</b><br>random slopes"] --> S7["<b>Step 7</b><br>equivalence"]
  end
  V["<b>Step 8</b><br>what follows"]
  MODEL --> EFFECTS
  EFFECTS --> ROBUST
  ROBUST --> V
  classDef both fill:#f0eaf8,stroke:#8e6bbf,color:#1d1d1f
  classDef verdict fill:#ffffff,stroke:#1d1d1f,color:#1d1d1f
  class S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6,S7 both
  class V verdict
  style MODEL fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style EFFECTS fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style ROBUST fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a






The eight steps in detail:
The model:

The model. The preregistered multilevel model, outcome ~ Occasion * condition + (1 | Municipality/id): wave (T0 to T3) and condition as fixed effects with their interaction, and random intercepts for persons nested in municipalities, fitted by REML. The fixed effects are tested with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom (lmerTest). The intercept is the control group in January, conditionExperimental the difference of the experimental group in January, OccasionT1 to OccasionT3 the change of the control group since January. The model then goes through the textbook checks of a multilevel model (Zuur et al., 2009, ch. 5; Harrison et al., 2018): the estimation converged, and two other optimizers (bobyqa and Nelder-Mead) give the same fixed effects, the check lme4 recommends when it warns; no variance is estimated at zero (a singular fit); the residuals and the random intercepts of the persons are close enough to normal (skewness within ±2, excess kurtosis below 7; West, Finch & Curran, 1995); and the residuals spread about evenly over the eight cells of condition and wave, shown with a figure of the residuals against the normal distribution and against the fitted values.
The random structure. Whether the municipality is a level of its own: the null model with persons nested in municipalities against persons alone, compared by AIC (lower is better), and how the variance is shared between municipalities, persons and the questionnaires of a person. The municipality level stays whatever AIC says: the conditions were assigned by municipality, so the design calls for it. Then the trainers, whom the preregistration names, together with their municipalities, as the random factor. Each trainer trained one municipality in each condition, so the municipalities are nested in the trainers. The model of step 1 with this further level is fitted with the bobyqa optimizer (with the default one, three of the 26 models stop short of convergence) and compared with the model of step 1 by AIC.

The effects:

The interactions. Each interaction term OccasionTk:conditionExperimental compares the change from T0 to wave k between the groups (positive: the experimental group changes more), tested two-sided at α = .05, with and without the trainer level. The expectation: positive at T1 and T2, once the experimental group has trained and the control group not yet, and near zero at T3, after both have trained. A figure shows the means the model implies for both groups at each wave.
One-sided tests. The hypotheses are directional. A one-sided test looks only in the expected direction: it halves the p of an effect that points there and gives an effect against the expectation a p above .5. Everywhere else the verdicts rest on two-sided tests; step 5 shows the one-sided p beside them. The correction for testing many outcomes at once needs the tests of all outcomes and follows in 10.7.
The replication. Whether the control group gains when it trains, in two models. The period-specific model uses only the September and December waves, with condition × T3 (negative when the control group gains more); singular fits, where a variance is estimated at zero, are marked. The piecewise model uses all four waves, with one time indicator for each training (Chapter 2): conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training is the effect while the experimental group trains (T0 to T1, expected positive), conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training the effect while the control group trains (T2 to T3, expected negative). For the composites a third model has a single indicator of being trained.

Robustness:

Random slopes. Time is coded by Helmert contrasts (T0 against later waves; T3 against earlier waves, Chapter 2). Within one condition every municipality had the same schedule, so slope variance there is free of the training effect. In each condition separately, four likelihood-ratio tests on maximum-likelihood fits:

random slopes of both contrasts across municipalities, against random intercepts. Within one condition each trainer worked in exactly one municipality, so trainers and municipalities are the same ten groups and one level stands for both;
a random slope across persons, for each contrast on its own: both at once would need more random effects than there are questionnaires;
a fixed interaction of municipality and pre/post in the arm’s own training window (T0 to T1 in the experimental group, T2 to T3 in the control group): do the ten municipalities gain differently from their training?

Slope variances near zero make single optimizers stop at different points, so every model is fitted with three and the best fit is kept. For the composites, random slopes of both contrasts at the trainer and municipality levels are also tested across both conditions.
Equivalence. Two claims of the preregistration are claims of absence: the groups do not differ at baseline (condition at T0), and they no longer differ after both have trained (condition × T3). A non-significant test does not show absence; two one-sided tests (TOST) do, against a smallest effect of interest of Δd = ±0.20. Each coefficient of the model of step 1 is divided by the standard deviation of the outcome at T0. Equivalence holds when the 90 % confidence interval lies within ±0.20. The verdict sets the TOST beside the two-sided test: equivalent (only the TOST is significant), different but trivially small (both are), different (only the two-sided test is) or inconclusive (neither is). The same tests follow with another rule for the random structure, the richest whose variances all lie above zero: persons in municipalities in trainers, else persons in municipalities, else persons alone (fitted with bobyqa).

What follows:

What follows. Where the result of the outcome goes next.

After the last outcome, 10.7 corrects the directional tests for the number of outcomes tested at once, and 10.8 sets all outcomes side by side.

title: 10. Multilevel models
text:
10.2 Data and tools
Which data? All questionnaires (df, Chapter 2) for every model except the period-specific one of step 5, which takes the September and December waves alone:

# the 26 outcomes: the 23 scales and the three hypothesis composites
composites <- c("H1_ListeningTogetherness", "H2_CognitiveComplexity",
                "H3_Wellbeing")
outcomes   <- c(scales$scale, composites)

# the September and December waves, with an indicator of December
df_T23 <- df |>
  filter(Occasion %in% c("T2", "T3")) |>
  mutate(Time_T3 = if_else(Occasion == "T3", 1, 0))

# the smallest effect of interest of the equivalence tests (step 7)
sesoi <- .20

The slopes within the conditions (step 6) are 208 likelihood-ratio tests: 26 outcomes, two conditions, four tests, every model fitted with three optimizers. They take more than a minute and run as a script; each outcome section reads its eight tests from the result:

# Random slopes within each condition (Chapter 10.5): for the 23 scales and
# the three composites, in each condition separately, whether the change
# varies between municipalities and between persons, and whether the
# municipalities change differently in their own training window.
# Likelihood-ratio tests on maximum-likelihood fits (about 1.5 minutes).
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapter 2:  Rscript scripts/slopes_within.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
df <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")      # one row per questionnaire (Chapter 2)
item_names <- names(select(df, ListenOther1:CompetenceNonFrustrated4))
source("R/scales.R")               # the 23 scales (Chapter 2)

outcomes <- c(scales$scale, "H1_ListeningTogetherness",
              "H2_CognitiveComplexity", "H3_Wellbeing")
time     <- "TF_helmert + TS_helmert"   # the two time contrasts (Chapter 2)

# each arm's own training window: T0 to T1 (experimental), T2 to T3 (control)
training_window <- list(Experimental = c("T0", "T1"),
                        Control      = c("T2", "T3"))

# a maximum-likelihood fit with three optimizers, keeping the best: with slope
# variances near zero, single optimizers stop at different points
ml_fit <- \(formula, data) {
  fits <- map(c("bobyqa", "Nelder_Mead", "nloptwrap"), \(optimizer)
    suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
      lmer(as.formula(formula), data = data, REML = FALSE,
           control = lmerControl(optimizer = optimizer)))))
  fits[[which.max(map_dbl(fits, logLik))]]
}

# likelihood-ratio test of a model against the same model with more terms
lr_test <- \(data, outcome, base, extended) {
  m0 <- ml_fit(str_c(outcome, " ~ ", base), data)
  m1 <- ml_fit(str_c(outcome, " ~ ", extended), data)
  chisq <- max(2 * (as.numeric(logLik(m1)) - as.numeric(logLik(m0))), 0)
  df    <- attr(logLik(m1), "df") - attr(logLik(m0), "df")
  tibble(chisq = chisq, df = df, p = pchisq(chisq, df, lower.tail = FALSE))
}

# the four tests of one outcome in one condition
within_condition <- \(outcome, group) {
  data <- df |>
    filter(condition == group) |>
    drop_na(all_of(outcome))
  window <- training_window[[group]]
  in_window <- data |>
    filter(Occasion %in% window) |>
    mutate(post = as.integer(Occasion == window[2]))
  bind_rows(
    "slopes, municipalities" = lr_test(data, outcome,
      str_c(time, " + (1 | Municipality) + (1 | id)"),
      str_c(time, " + (", time, " | Municipality) + (1 | id)")),
    "slope T0 vs. later, persons" = lr_test(data, outcome,
      str_c(time, " + (1 | id)"),
      str_c(time, " + (1 + TF_helmert | id)")),
    "slope T3 vs. earlier, persons" = lr_test(data, outcome,
      str_c(time, " + (1 | id)"),
      str_c(time, " + (1 + TS_helmert | id)")),
    "municipality x pre/post" = lr_test(in_window, outcome,
      "Municipality + post + (1 | id)",
      "Municipality * post + (1 | id)"),
    .id = "test")
}

slopes_within <- expand_grid(outcome   = outcomes,
                             condition = c("Experimental", "Control")) |>
  mutate(tests = map2(outcome, condition, within_condition)) |>
  unnest(tests)

saveRDS(slopes_within, "cache/slopes_within.rds")


slopes_within <- readRDS("cache/slopes_within.rds")

Which tools? The analysis of each step is written out for every outcome. The checks of Step 1, the path at the head of each outcome, the figure, the verdict of the equivalence tests, the names in the text and the tables that bring the outcomes together use small functions, defined once here:

Model checksPathModel-implied meansVerdictsNamesAll outcomesTables at a glance



# ✓ or ✗
mark <- \(x) if_else(x, "✓", "✗")

# skewness and excess kurtosis of a set of values
skew_of     <- \(x) mean((x - mean(x))^3) / sd(x)^3
kurtosis_of <- \(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / sd(x)^4 - 3

# whether a fit converged without lme4's warning
converges <- \(fit) {
  !any(str_detect(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages %||% "", "converge"))
}

# the same model with two other optimizers: do they converge, and how far
# do their fixed effects lie from those of the model? (the check lme4
# recommends when it warns; see its help page on convergence)
other_optimizers <- \(fit) {
  refits <- c("bobyqa", "Nelder_Mead") |>
    set_names() |>
    map(\(optimizer) lmer(formula(fit), data = fit@frame,
                          control = lmerControl(optimizer = optimizer)))
  tibble(converge = all(map_lgl(refits, converges)),
         distance = max(map_dbl(refits, \(refit)
           max(abs(lme4::fixef(refit) - lme4::fixef(fit))))))
}

# the textbook checks of a multilevel model (Zuur et al., 2009, ch. 5;
# Harrison et al., 2018): did the estimation converge, and do two other
# optimizers give the same fixed effects; is no variance estimated at zero
# (a singular fit); are the residuals and the person intercepts close
# enough to normal (skewness within ±2, excess kurtosis below 7; West,
# Finch & Curran, 1995); and how evenly do the residuals spread over the
# eight cells of condition and wave
lmm_checks <- \(fit) {
  residuals <- residuals(fit)
  persons   <- ranef(fit)[[str_subset(names(ranef(fit)), "^id")[1]]][[1]]
  others    <- other_optimizers(fit)
  smallest  <- as_tibble(VarCorr(fit)) |>
    filter(grp != "Residual") |>
    slice_min(sdcor, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  spread    <- tibble(residual = residuals,
                      cell = interaction(model.frame(fit)$condition,
                                         model.frame(fit)$Occasion)) |>
    summarise(sd = sd(residual), .by = cell)
  tribble(
    ~check, ~value, ~criterion, ~holds,
    "1 estimation: converged",
    if (converges(fit)) "yes" else "warning", "yes", converges(fit),
    "2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead",
    str_c(if (others$converge) "converge, " else "warning, ",
          "fixed effects within ", format(signif(others$distance, 1),
                                          scientific = FALSE)),
    "within .001", others$converge & others$distance < .001,
    "3 variances: none at zero",
    str_c("smallest SD ", sprintf("%.3f", smallest$sdcor), " (",
          str_remove(smallest$grp, ":Municipality"), ")"),
    "not singular", !isSingular(fit),
    "4 residuals: skewness", apa(skew_of(residuals), 2), "within ±2",
    abs(skew_of(residuals)) <= 2,
    "5 residuals: excess kurtosis", apa(kurtosis_of(residuals), 2),
    "below 7", kurtosis_of(residuals) < 7,
    "6 person intercepts: skewness", apa(skew_of(persons), 2),
    "within ±2", abs(skew_of(persons)) <= 2,
    "7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells",
    sprintf("%.2f", max(spread$sd) / min(spread$sd)), "reported", NA
  ) |>
    mutate(holds = if_else(is.na(holds), "–", mark(holds)))
}

# what the checks say, in two or three sentences
lmm_sentence <- \(checks) {
  fails <- \(k) checks$holds[str_starts(checks$check, as.character(k))] ==
    "✗"
  value <- \(k) checks$value[str_starts(checks$check, as.character(k))]
  ratio <- value(7)
  # the level of the smallest variance, in words
  level <- c(Municipality = "municipalities", id = "persons",
             trainedBy = "trainers")[str_match(value(3), "\\((.*)\\)")[, 2]]
  smallest_sd <- str_extract(value(3), "[0-9.]+")
  if (!any(checks$holds == "✗")) {
    return(str_c("The model converges, two other optimizers give the same ",
                 "fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the ",
                 "residuals and the person intercepts stay within the ",
                 "bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly ",
                 "over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is ",
                 ratio, " times the smallest)."))
  }
  c(if (fails(1) && !fails(2)) {
      str_c("lme4 warns that its default optimizer stopped short of ",
            "convergence. Bobyqa and Nelder-Mead fit the same model without ",
            "a warning and agree with it on every fixed effect, to ",
            str_extract(value(2), "within .*"), ": the warning comes from ",
            "the boundary, a variance close to zero (the SD between ",
            level, " is ", smallest_sd, "), not from estimates that are ",
            "off, and the model of step 1 stands.")
    },
    if (fails(1) && fails(2)) {
      str_c("The estimation stops short of convergence, and other ",
            "optimizers do not repair it (", value(2), ").")
    },
    if (fails(3)) {
      str_c("A variance is estimated at zero, between ", level, ": the model ",
            "reduces to a simpler random structure, which leaves the fixed ",
            "effects as they are; step 7 repeats the claims of absence ",
            "with the richest structure whose variances all lie above ",
            "zero.")
    },
    if (fails(4) || fails(5) || fails(6)) {
      shape <- c(if (fails(4)) str_c("the residuals are skewed (", value(4),
                                     ")"),
                 if (fails(5)) str_c("heavy-tailed (excess kurtosis ",
                                     value(5), ")"),
                 if (fails(6)) str_c("the person intercepts skewed (",
                                     value(6), ")")) |>
        str_flatten_comma(last = " and ")
      top <- str_starts(value(4), "-")
      str_c(str_replace(shape, "^t", "T"), ": the answers crowd at the ",
            if (top) "top" else "bottom", " of the scale. The fixed effects ",
            "and their tests are robust to such departures in samples of ",
            "this size (Schielzeth et al., 2020), but little room is left ",
            "for a change.")
    }) |>
    str_flatten(" ")
}

# the residuals of a model against the normal distribution, and against
# its fitted values
plot_residuals <- \(fit) {
  points <- tibble(residual = residuals(fit), fitted = fitted(fit))
  bind_rows(
    points |>
      arrange(residual) |>
      mutate(x = qnorm(ppoints(n())), y = residual,
             panel = "residuals against the normal"),
    points |> transmute(x = fitted, y = residual,
                        panel = "residuals against fitted values")) |>
    ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(size = .8, alpha = .35, colour = "#2a78d6") +
    geom_abline(data = tibble(panel = "residuals against the normal"),
                aes(intercept = 0, slope = sd(points$residual)),
                colour = "#e34948", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(data = tibble(panel = "residuals against fitted values"),
               aes(yintercept = 0), colour = "#e34948",
               linetype = "dashed") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "residual") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}




# an estimate with its p, as "b = 0.52, p = .003"
b_text <- \(b, p) str_c("b = ", sprintf("%.2f", b), ", p = ", apa(p, 3))

# the path of an outcome through the eight steps: the models of the steps,
# fitted here once more with the same formulas
outcome_path <- \(outcome, next_text) {
  model_of <- \(right, data = df, ...) {
    lmer(as.formula(str_c(outcome, " ~ ", right)), data = data, ...)
  }
  model   <- model_of("Occasion * condition + (1 | Municipality/id)")
  trainer <- model_of("Occasion * condition + (1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)",
                      control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  aic_municipality <- AIC(model_of("1 + (1 | id)")) -
    AIC(model_of("1 + (1 | Municipality/id)"))
  aic_trainer <- AIC(trainer) - AIC(model)
  terms <- tidy(model, effects = "fixed")
  interactions <- terms |> filter(str_detect(term, ":"))
  period <- model_of("condition * Time_T3 + (1 | Municipality/id)",
                     data = df_T23) |>
    tidy(effects = "fixed") |>
    filter(str_detect(term, ":"))
  piecewise <- model_of(str_c("condition * (Time_Exp_Training + ",
                              "Time_Control_Training) + ",
                              "(1 | Municipality/id)")) |>
    tidy(effects = "fixed") |>
    filter(str_detect(term, "Control_Training"), str_detect(term, ":"))
  slopes <- slopes_within |> filter(outcome == .env$outcome)
  sd_T0 <- sd(df[[outcome]][df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)
  claims <- terms |>
    filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                       "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
    mutate(d = estimate / sd_T0, se_d = std.error / sd_T0,
           p_tost = pmax(pt((d + sesoi) / se_d, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
                         pt((d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
           verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p.value))
  checks <- lmm_checks(model)
  failing <- str_extract(checks$check[checks$holds == "✗"], "^[0-9]+")
  problems <- c(`1` = "a convergence warning", `2` = "optimizers disagree",
                `3` = "a variance at zero", `4` = "skewed residuals",
                `5` = "heavy-tailed residuals",
                `6` = "skewed person intercepts")
  tribble(
    ~Step, ~Question, ~Result, ~Next,
    "1", "Does the model pass the textbook checks?",
    if (length(failing) == 0) {
      "yes, all six"
    } else if (identical(failing, "1")) {
      str_c("a convergence warning, a false alarm: two other optimizers ",
            "agree")
    } else {
      str_flatten_comma(problems[failing], last = " and ")
    }, "random structure",
    "2", "Municipalities a level of their own? Trainers?",
    str_c(if (aic_municipality > 0) "municipalities: yes" else
            "municipalities: not by AIC, kept by design",
          "; trainers: ", if (aic_trainer < 0) "AIC lower" else "no"),
    "interactions",
    "3", "Does the experimental group change more (T1, T2, T3)?",
    str_c(str_extract(interactions$term, "T[1-3]"), ": ",
          b_text(interactions$estimate, interactions$p.value)) |>
      str_flatten("; "),
    "one-sided tests",
    "5", "Does the control group gain more while it trains?",
    str_c("September to December: ", b_text(period$estimate, period$p.value),
          "; piecewise: ", b_text(piecewise$estimate, piecewise$p.value)),
    "random slopes",
    "6", "Does the change vary within a condition?",
    str_c(sum(slopes$p < .05), " of ", nrow(slopes), " tests significant"),
    "equivalence",
    "7", "Alike at baseline and after both trainings (TOST)?",
    str_c("baseline: ", claims$verdict[1], "; after both: ",
          claims$verdict[2]), "what follows",
    "8", "Where next?", next_text, "")
}




# the means the model implies for both conditions at each wave; shaded the
# two training windows (experimental: T0 to T1, control: T2 to T3)
plot_means <- \(fit) {
  cells <- expand_grid(Occasion  = factor(c("T0", "T1", "T2", "T3")),
                       condition = factor(c("Control", "Experimental")))
  cells |>
    mutate(mean = predict(fit, newdata = cells, re.form = NA),
           wave = as.integer(Occasion) - 1) |>
    ggplot(aes(wave, mean, colour = condition)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#eb6834", alpha = .08) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 2, xmax = 3, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .08) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 2.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Control      = "#2a78d6",
                                   Experimental = "#eb6834")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:3,
                       labels = str_c("T", 0:3, "\n", months_list)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "model-implied mean", colour = NULL,
         caption = str_c("shaded: the training of the experimental group ",
                         "(left) and of the control group (right)")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
}




# the verdict of an equivalence test, next to the two-sided test
verdict_of <- \(p_tost, p_two_sided) case_when(
  p_tost < .05 & p_two_sided >= .05 ~ "equivalent",
  p_tost < .05                      ~ "different but trivially small",
  p_two_sided < .05                 ~ "different",
  .default                          = "inconclusive"
)

composite_labels <- c(H1_ListeningTogetherness = "Listening and Togetherness",

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows
Where does the result go? Well-being reaches significance at T1 and T2 only one-sided, and in the experimental group’s window of the piecewise model; the control group does not gain significantly more when it trains. Its interaction at T1 is the preregistered test of Hypothesis 3: 10.7 corrects it within the three composites, Chapter 14 repeats the model in every sample set, and Chapter 20 sets it beside the other estimates of the training effect.

title: 10. Multilevel models
text:
10.7 Many outcomes at once
Which tests are corrected? Each hypothesis is tested on many outcomes at once. The directional tests of the 26 sections come together in three tables: the interactions (step 3), the period-specific terms and the piecewise terms (step 5):

interactions <- from_sections("interactions") |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "outcome") |>
  transmute(outcome, term, b, se, df, p,
            wave = str_extract(term, "T[1-3]"))

period_specific <- from_sections("period_terms") |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "outcome") |>
  select(outcome, singular, term, b, se, df, p)

piecewise <- from_sections("piecewise_terms") |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "outcome") |>
  mutate(training = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), "experimental",
                            "control"))

With which sign? The experimental group should gain more by T1 and keep its advantage at T2 (positive interactions); the control group should gain more while it trains (negative terms in the period-specific model and in the second term of the piecewise model), while the first piecewise term should be positive. The one-sided p as in step 4:

# the directional tests of steps 3 and 5, with the sign they expect
directional <- bind_rows(
  interactions |>
    filter(wave %in% c("T1", "T2")) |>
    transmute(test = str_c("preregistered, ", wave), outcome, b, se, df, p,
              expected = 1),
  period_specific |>
    transmute(test = "period-specific, T3", outcome, b, se, df, p,
              expected = -1),
  piecewise |>
    transmute(test = str_c("piecewise, ", training, " training"), outcome,
              b, se, df, p,
              expected = if_else(training == "experimental", 1, -1))
) |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

Does the result hold if the p-values are corrected for testing many outcomes? The Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each test, over the 23 scales and, as a family of their own, over the three composites (one per hypothesis); for the two-sided and for the one-sided p:

directional <- directional |>
  mutate(family = if_else(outcome %in% scales$scale, "scales",
                          "composites")) |>
  mutate(p_BH           = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
         p_one_sided_BH = p.adjust(p_one_sided, method = "BH"),
         .by = c(test, family))

And the random structure and the claims of absence? First the null models, the trainer level and the equivalence tests of the 26 sections, each brought together in one table:

  outcome    = outcomes,
  AIC_nested = unname(map_dbl(from_sections("null_nested"), AIC)),
  AIC_person = unname(map_dbl(from_sections("null_person"), AIC))) |>
  mutate(better = if_else(AIC_nested <= AIC_person, "Municipality/id",
                          "id"))

trainer_shares <- from_sections("trainer_shares") |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "outcome") |>
  filter(level == "trainedBy") |>
  select(outcome, trainer_share = share)

trainer_comparison <- tibble(
  outcome          = outcomes,
  AIC_municipality = unname(map_dbl(from_sections("model"), AIC)),
  AIC_trainer      = unname(map_dbl(from_sections("trainer"), AIC))) |>
  left_join(trainer_shares, by = "outcome")

both_structures <- from_sections("interactions") |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "outcome") |>
  transmute(outcome, wave = str_extract(term, "T[1-3]"), b, p, b_trainer,
            p_trainer)

# both structures of step 7; per outcome first the claim after both
# trainings, then the one at baseline

  arrange(match(outcome, outcomes), claim)

  filter(model == "preregistered") |>
  select(outcome, claim, term, delta_d, se_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost,
         p_two_sided, verdict)

richest_structures <- tibble(
  outcome   = outcomes,
  structure = as.character(from_sections("richest")))

  filter(model == "richest") |>
  left_join(richest_structures, by = "outcome") |>
  select(outcome, structure, claim, term, delta_d, se_d, ci_low, ci_high,
         p_tost, p_two_sided, verdict)

AIC prefers the models without the trainer level for 25 of the 26 outcomes; only for Flourishing does the trainer level lower it, by 1.0 points. The interaction terms move by at most 0.008 and no test changes its verdict, so the counts of significant effects hold with either structure; step 7 of each outcome finds the same for the equivalence tests.
What do the interactions show across the outcomes?
At T1, 10 scales show a significant interaction in favour of the experimental group, led by Others Listen to Me, Paradox Mindset, and I Listen (b = 0.82, 0.71, 0.60); No Alienation again moves against the training (b = -0.76).
