title: 12. Serial mediation
text:
12.1 How each window is examined
How does the training reach well-being? In each window, the composite scores at the end of the window are regressed in sequence: H1 on the training, H2 on H1 and the training, H3 on H2, H1 and the training. All three regressions control for the three composites at the start of the window. The indirect effect on H3 splits into three paths: through H1 alone, through H2 alone, and through H1 and H2 in series. Within a wave, H1, H2 and H3 are measured at the same time; their order inside the wave is a theoretical assumption, not a feature of the design.
Which windows? Four: the experimental group trains (Model 1, T0 to T1), durability from baseline (Model 2, T0 to T2), maintenance without new training (Model 3, T1 to T2, which controls for a state already after the training and is read with care), and the replication while the control group trains (Model 4, T2 to T3, with train_cg in place of train_eg).
What happens to each window? The same seven steps, in the same order and in four parts: the model, the effects, their robustness, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.





flowchart TB
  subgraph MODEL["the model"]
    direction LR
    S1["<b>Step 1</b><br>the model"] --> S2{{"<b>Step 2</b><br>path diagram:<br>possible? does it fit?"}}
  end
  subgraph EFFECTS["the effects"]
    direction LR
    S3["<b>Step 3</b><br>the paths a, b, c"] --> S4["<b>Step 4</b><br>the indirect effects"]
  end
  subgraph ROBUST["robustness"]
    direction LR
    S5["<b>Step 5</b><br>complete cases,<br>clustered errors"] --> S6["<b>Step 6</b><br>latent blocks"]
  end
  V["<b>Step 7</b><br>what follows"]
  MODEL --> EFFECTS
  EFFECTS --> ROBUST
  ROBUST --> V
  classDef all fill:#efeff2,stroke:#8a8a8a,color:#1d1d1f
  classDef verdict fill:#ffffff,stroke:#1d1d1f,color:#1d1d1f
  class S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6 all
  class V verdict
  style MODEL fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style EFFECTS fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style ROBUST fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a






The seven steps in detail:
The model:

The model. Its lavaan syntax, written out: the three regressions with the paths a (training → H1), b1 (H1 → H2), b2 (training → H2), c1 (H2 → H3), c2 (H1 → H3) and c3 (training → H3), and the indirect, direct and total effects defined from them. Each model is fitted by maximum likelihood with 1,000 bootstrap draws, once with full information (FIML, all persons) and once with complete cases only.
The path diagram. The six paths, standardized (FIML), with stars for p < .05, .01 and .001, and the fit of the model. The model keeps three degrees of freedom: it takes the training to be unrelated to the three composites at the start of the window. Where this holds, the model fits closely (χ² test with p above .05, CFI from .95, SRMR below .08). Before the paths are read, the model goes through the textbook checks of a path model, in the order of Chapter 7 (Kline, 2016, ch. 9): the estimation converged, no variance is negative, no correlation lies beyond ±1, every parameter has a standard error, and the fit by χ², CFI, RMSEA (up to .06) and SRMR (Hu & Bentler, 1999).

The effects:

The paths a, b and c. Their standardized estimates, standard errors and p-values.
The indirect effects. Indirect, direct and total effects, unstandardized, with bias-corrected bootstrap intervals (95 %) and the p-value of a z-test on the bootstrap standard error. An effect carries when its interval excludes 0. The z-test assumes that an estimate is normally distributed across samples; an indirect effect is a product of paths, and the distribution of a product is skewed. The bootstrap interval, which follows the skew, is therefore the standard test for indirect effects (MacKinnon et al., 2004; Preacher & Hayes, 2008), and it decides here. Where the two tests disagree, the bootstrap draws of the effect show why. An indirect effect that carries while the direct path does not is an indirect-only mediation (Zhao et al., 2010).

Robustness:

Complete cases and clustered errors. How many persons carry the window, and whether the paths and effects keep their significance with complete cases only (bootstrap) and with standard errors clustered by municipality, where the training was assigned (no bootstrap). The key paths are a, b1 and c1, which make up the serial path.
Latent blocks. The same model with each block as a latent factor measured by its scale scores, estimated by local structural-after-measurement (SAM; Rosseel & Loh, 2024): how well the scales measure each block (against the CFI of .90 that the block models of Chapter 8 have to meet), which effects carry, and how large they are, standardized, against the composites.

What follows:

What follows. What the window adds to the pathway, and where its results go.

# the four windows and the group that trains in each
mediation_windows <- tribble(
  ~model, ~pre, ~post, ~treated,   ~reading,
  1,      "T0", "T1",  "train_eg", "the experimental group trains",
  2,      "T0", "T2",  "train_eg", "durability from baseline",
  3,      "T1", "T2",  "train_eg", "maintenance, no new training",
  4,      "T2", "T3",  "train_cg", "the control group trains (replication)"
)

# the wide names of the composites at a wave: T1_Hypothesis2_... and so on
composite_at <- \(wave) {
  str_c(wave, "_", c("Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness",
                     "Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity",
                     "Hypothesis3_Wellbeing"))
}

mediation_model <- \(pre, post, treated) {
  before   <- composite_at(pre)
  after    <- composite_at(post)
  controls <- str_c(before, collapse = " + ")
  c(
    # paths: a (training -> H1), b1 and b2 (-> H2), c1 to c3 (-> H3)
    str_c(after[1], " ~ A*", treated, " + ", controls),
    str_c(after[2], " ~ B1*", after[1], " + B2*", treated, " + ", controls),
    str_c(after[3], " ~ C1*", after[2], " + C2*", after[1], " + C3*",
          treated, " + ", controls),
    # the controls covary
    str_c(before[1], " ~~ ", before[2]),
    str_c(before[1], " ~~ ", before[3]),
    str_c(before[2], " ~~ ", before[3]),
    # effects on H2
    "indirectH2 := A*B1",
    "directH2 := B2",
    "totalH2 := B2 + A*B1",
    # effects on H3: via H1, via H2, via both in series
    "ind_LET := A*C2",
    "ind_CF := B2*C1",
    "ind_serial := A*B1*C1",
    "total_indirect := A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1",
    "directH3 := C3",
    "totalH3 := C3 + A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1"
  ) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# maximum likelihood with 1,000 bootstrap draws (seed as before); missing
# values by full information ("fiml") or complete cases ("listwise")
fit_mediation <- \(model, data, missing = "fiml") {
  set.seed(20260525)
  sem(model, data = data, estimator = "ML", se = "bootstrap",
      bootstrap = 1000, missing = missing)
}




# Serial mediation: the bootstrapped fits of Chapter 12, four windows, full
# information and complete cases, 1,000 draws each (about 6 minutes)
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapter 2:  Rscript scripts/mediation_bootstrap.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
source("R/mediation_model.R")
df_wide <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds")   # one row per person (Chapter 2)

mediation <- mediation_windows |>
  mutate(syntax   = pmap_chr(list(pre, post, treated), mediation_model),
         fiml     = map(syntax, \(m) fit_mediation(m, df_wide)),
         listwise = map(syntax, \(m) fit_mediation(m, df_wide, "listwise")))

saveRDS(mediation, "cache/mediation_bootstrap.rds")




# Serial mediation with latent blocks (Chapter 12): each hypothesis block is
# a latent factor measured by its scale scores, estimated by local
# structural-after-measurement (SAM; Rosseel & Loh, 2024). Needs R/scales.R
# and R/mediation_model.R.

# one row per person, in the order of df_wide: the 23 scale scores at each
# wave (ListenOther_T0, ...) and the two training indicators
scale_scores_wide <- \(data, wide) {
  scores <- data |>
    select(id, Occasion, all_of(scales$scale)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Occasion, values_from = all_of(scales$scale),
                names_glue = "{.value}_{Occasion}")
  wide |>
    select(id, train_eg, train_cg) |>
    left_join(scores, by = "id")
}

sam_blocks <- list(H1 = h1_scales, H2 = h2_scales, H3 = h3_scales)

# scales of reverse-keyed items only: their residuals share the wording
reverse_keyed <- c("NoAlienation", "NoIsolation", "AutonomyNonFrustrated",
                   "RelatednessNonFrustrated", "CompetenceNonFrustrated")

# one block at the two waves of a window: the first scale is the marker,
# the loadings are equal over the two waves, each scale's residual covaries
# with itself over the waves and with the other reverse-keyed scales
measurement_block <- \(block, waves) {
  s      <- sam_blocks[[block]]
  labels <- c("1*", str_c(str_to_lower(block), "_", seq_along(s)[-1], "*"))
  keyed  <- intersect(s, reverse_keyed)
  wording <- if (length(keyed) < 2) character() else
    map(waves, \(w) combn(keyed, 2, \(p)
      str_c(p[1], "_", w, " ~~ ", p[2], "_", w))) |> unlist()
  c(map_chr(waves, \(w) str_c(block, "_", w, " =~ ",
                              str_c(labels, s, "_", w, collapse = " + "))),
    str_c(s, "_", waves[1], " ~~ ", s, "_", waves[2]),
    wording)
}

# the measurement blocks and the structural model of 12.1, with the
# composites replaced by the latent blocks (T1_Hypothesis2_... -> H2_T1)
sam_mediation_model <- \(pre, post, treated) {
  structural <- mediation_model(pre, post, treated) |>
    str_replace_all("(T[0-3])_Hypothesis([1-3])_[A-Za-z]+", "H\\2_\\1")
  c(map(names(sam_blocks), \(b) measurement_block(b, c(pre, post))) |>
      unlist(),
    structural) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# the measurement blocks of a window: each block at both waves together
sam_mm_list <- \(pre, post) {
  map(names(sam_blocks), \(b) str_c(b, "_", c(pre, post))) |>
    set_names(names(sam_blocks))
}

# local SAM, missing values by full information (with enough EM steps for
# the saturated moments, as in Chapter 8), 1,000 bootstrap draws (seed as
# in Chapter 12)
fit_sam_mediation <- \(model, data, pre, post) {
  set.seed(20260525)
  sam(model, data = data, mm.list = sam_mm_list(pre, post),
      missing = "fiml", em.h1.iter.max = 20000, se = "bootstrap",
      bootstrap.args = list(R = 1000L))
}

# the fit of each measurement block, the first step of SAM on its own
measurement_fit <- \(model, data, pre, post) {
  steps <- sam(model, data = data, mm.list = sam_mm_list(pre, post),
               missing = "fiml", em.h1.iter.max = 20000, se = "none",
               output = "list")
  steps$MM.FIT |>
    set_names(names(sam_blocks)) |>
    map(\(f) fitMeasures(f, c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr")) |>
          as.list() |>
          as_tibble()) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "block")
}

# quantiles of bootstrap draws, interpolated on the normal scale between
# neighbouring order statistics (as lavaan's percentile intervals)
draw_quantile <- \(draws, probs) {
  t <- sort(draws[is.finite(draws)])
  n <- length(t)
  map_dbl(probs, \(p) {
    k <- trunc((n + 1) * p)
    if (k < 1) return(t[1])
    if (k >= n) return(t[n])
    z <- qnorm(c(p, k / (n + 1), (k + 1) / (n + 1)))
    t[k] + (z[1] - z[2]) / (z[3] - z[2]) * (t[k + 1] - t[k])
  })
}

# the bias-corrected percentile interval of bootstrap draws, computed as
# lavaan's boot.ci.type = "bca.simple"
bc_interval <- \(draws, estimate, level = .95) {
  z0 <- qnorm(mean(draws < estimate))
  draw_quantile(draws, pnorm(2 * z0 + qnorm((1 + c(-level, level)) / 2)))
}

# the defined effects of a SAM fit: each effect's formula (A*B1*C1, ...) on
# the estimates and on every bootstrap draw
sam_effects <- \(fit) {
  draws <- as.data.frame(lavInspect(fit, "boot"))
  parameterEstimates(fit, se = FALSE, zstat = FALSE, pvalue = FALSE,
                     ci = FALSE) |>
    filter(op == ":=") |>
    mutate(ci = map2(rhs, est, \(f, e)
      bc_interval(eval(str2lang(f), draws), e))) |>
    transmute(effect = label, est, ci_low = map_dbl(ci, 1),
              ci_high = map_dbl(ci, 2))
}




# Serial mediation with latent blocks (Chapter 12): local SAM in the four
# windows, 1,000 bootstrap draws each (about an hour)
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapter 2:  Rscript scripts/mediation_sam.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
df      <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")        # one row per questionnaire
df_wide <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds")   # one row per person
item_names <- names(select(df, ListenOther1:CompetenceNonFrustrated4))
source("R/scales.R")
source("R/mediation_model.R")
source("R/mediation_sam.R")
scores <- scale_scores_wide(df, df_wide)

mediation_sam <- mediation_windows |>
  mutate(syntax = pmap_chr(list(pre, post, treated), sam_mediation_model),
         fit    = pmap(list(syntax, pre, post), \(m, a, b)
           fit_sam_mediation(m, scores, a, b)))

saveRDS(mediation_sam, "cache/mediation_sam.rds")




The FIML fits include all 451 persons; those without any answer in a window carry no information on it and leave the estimates unchanged.
Which tools? The analysis of each step is written out for every window. Only the checks of Step 2, the labels, the figures and the table of the three estimators use small functions, defined once here:

ChecksLabelsPath diagramBootstrap drawsEstimatorsEffects across windows



# ✓ or ✗
mark <- \(x) if_else(x, "✓", "✗")

# the textbook checks of a path model (Kline, 2016, ch. 9), in the order of
# Chapter 7: did the estimation converge, is the solution proper, and how
# well does the model fit (χ² test with p above .05, CFI from .95, RMSEA up
# to .06 and SRMR below .08; Hu & Bentler, 1999)
path_checks <- \(fit) {
  variances <- parameterEstimates(fit) |> filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs)
  correlations <- standardizedSolution(fit, se = FALSE, zstat = FALSE,
                                       pvalue = FALSE, ci = FALSE) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs)
  se <- parTable(fit) |> filter(free > 0) |> pull(se)
  fm <- fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea",
                           "srmr"))
  tribble(
    ~check, ~value, ~criterion, ~holds,
    "1 estimation: converged",
    if (lavInspect(fit, "converged")) "yes" else "no", "yes",
    lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
    "2 variances: smallest variance", apa(min(variances$est), 3),
    "above 0", min(variances$est) > 0,
    "3 correlations: largest", apa(max(abs(correlations$est.std)), 2),
    "within ±1", max(abs(correlations$est.std)) <= 1,
    "4 standard errors", if (all(is.finite(se) & se > 0)) "yes" else "no",
    "yes", all(is.finite(se) & se > 0),
    "5 fit: χ² test",
    str_c("χ²(", fm[["df"]], ") = ", sprintf("%.2f", fm[["chisq"]]),
          ", p = ", apa(fm[["pvalue"]], 3)),
    "p above .05", fm[["pvalue"]] > .05,
    "6 fit: CFI", apa(fm[["cfi"]], 3), "at least .95", fm[["cfi"]] >= .95,
    "7 fit: RMSEA", apa(fm[["rmsea"]], 3), "at most .06",
    fm[["rmsea"]] <= .06,
    "8 fit: SRMR", apa(fm[["srmr"]], 3), "below .08", fm[["srmr"]] < .08
  ) |>
    mutate(holds = mark(holds))
}

# what the checks say, in one sentence
path_sentence <- \(checks) {
  proper <- all(checks$holds[1:4] == "✓")
  misfit <- checks |> slice(5:8) |> filter(holds == "✗")
  str_c(if (proper) {
          "The estimation converges and the solution is proper"
        } else "The solution is not proper",
        if (nrow(misfit) == 0) {
          ", and the model fits closely by all four indices."
        } else {
          str_c(", but it misses ",
                str_flatten_comma(str_c("the ", str_remove(misfit$check,
                                                           "^[0-9] fit: ")),
                                  last = " and "),
                ": the model's assumption that the training is unrelated ",
                "to the composites at the start of the window does not ",
                "hold here, and the window is read with care.")
        })
}




# the names of the effects and paths in the tables
effect_labels <- c(
  indirectH2     = "H2: indirect via H1 (a × b1)",
  directH2       = "H2: direct (b2)",
  totalH2        = "H2: total",
  ind_LET        = "H3: indirect via H1 (a × c2)",
  ind_CF         = "H3: indirect via H2 (b2 × c1)",
  ind_serial     = "H3: serial via H1 and H2 (a × b1 × c1)",
  total_indirect = "H3: total indirect",
  directH3       = "H3: direct (c3)",
  totalH3        = "H3: total"
)
path_labels <- c(A = "a: training -> H1", B1 = "b1: H1 -> H2",
                 B2 = "b2: training -> H2", C1 = "c1: H2 -> H3",
                 C2 = "c2: H1 -> H3", C3 = "c3: training -> H3",
                 effect_labels)




# the fit beside the diagram, and its title above
fit_text <- \(fit, title = "") {
  values <- fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "tli",
                               "rmsea", "srmr"))
  labels <- c("ChiSq", "df", "p", "CFI", "TLI", "RMSEA", "SRMR")
  text(1.15, -.4, labels = str_c(labels, " = ", round(values, 3),
                                 collapse = "\n"),
       pos = 4, cex = .75)
  text(0, 1.4, labels = title, cex = 1)
}

# the six paths of a window as a path diagram: the training, and H1, H2
# and H3 at the end of the window (the composites at its start, which all
# regressions control for, are left out); standardized estimates, stars
# for their significance
mediationPlot <- \(fit, title) {
  ends     <- lavNames(fit, "eqs.y")  # H1, H2 and H3 at the end
  training <- lavNames(fit, "ov.x")   # train_eg or train_cg
  starts   <- setdiff(lavNames(fit, "ov"), c(ends, training))
  semPlotModel(fit) |>
    drop_nodes(starts) |>
    semPaths(whatLabels = "std", style = "mx",
             layout = matrix(c(NA,       ends[1], ends[2], NA,
                               training, NA,      NA,      ends[3]),
                             nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
             nCharNodes = 0, edge.color = "black", intercepts = FALSE,
             asize = 2.5, sizeMan = 9, sizeMan2 = 6, edge.label.cex = .8,
             mar = c(3, 2, 5, 9), DoNotPlot = TRUE) |>
    mark_sig(fit, std_type = TRUE) |>
    change_node_label(set_names(c(str_c(c("H1", "H2", "H3"), "\n",
                                        str_sub(ends, 1, 2)),
                                  "Training"),
                                c(ends, training)),
                      label.cex = 1) |>
    plot()
  fit_text(fit, title)
}




# the bootstrap draws of one effect (bars), the normal curve the z-test
# assumes (centred on the estimate, with the bootstrap standard error),
# the bias-corrected interval (dashed) and 0 (grey)
plot_draws <- \(draws, effect) {
  tibble(draw = as.numeric(draws)) |>
    ggplot(aes(draw)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40,
                   fill = "#2a78d6", colour = "white") +
    stat_function(fun = dnorm,
                  args = list(mean = effect$est, sd = sd(draws)),
                  colour = "#eb6834", linewidth = .8) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(effect$ci_low, effect$ci_high),
               linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .6) +
    labs(x = str_c("bootstrap draws: ", effect_labels[effect$effect]),
         y = "density") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}




# the standardized paths and effects of a fit, with their p-values
standardized <- \(fit) {
  standardizedSolution(fit) |>
    filter(label %in% names(path_labels)) |>
    distinct(label, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    transmute(label, beta = est.std, p = pvalue)
}




# the effects on well-being (H3) in each window, with their bias-corrected
# intervals; filled where the interval excludes 0
plot_effects <- \(effects) {
  effects |>
    filter(str_starts(as.character(effect), "H3")) |>
    mutate(effect     = fct_rev(fct_drop(effect)),
           window     = str_c("Model ", model, ": ", reading),
           excludes_0 = ci_low > 0 | ci_high < 0) |>
    ggplot(aes(est, effect)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high, shape = excludes_0),
                    colour = "#2a78d6", fill = "white", size = .4) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21),
                       guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~ window, ncol = 2) +
    labs(x = "effect on well-being (H3), with its 95 % interval", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model all persons
What is regressed on what? The experimental group trains between January (T0) and March (T1); train_eg marks the persons of its ten municipalities. The composites at T1 are regressed on the training and on each other, controlling for the composites at T0:

m1_model <- "
  # a: the training -> H1
  T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~ A*train_eg +
    T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # b1: H1 -> H2, b2: the training -> H2
  T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~ B1*T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness +
    B2*train_eg +
    T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # c1: H2 -> H3, c2: H1 -> H3, c3: the training -> H3
  T1_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing ~ C1*T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    C2*T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + C3*train_eg +
    T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the composites at T0 covary
  T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity
  T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~~ T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the effects on H2
  indirectH2 := A*B1
  directH2   := B2
  totalH2    := B2 + A*B1
  # the effects on H3: via H1, via H2, via both in series
  ind_LET        := A*C2
  ind_CF         := B2*C1
  ind_serial     := A*B1*C1
  total_indirect := A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
  directH3       := C3
  totalH3        := C3 + A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
"

Which fits? The script fitted this model with 1,000 bootstrap draws, once with all persons (FIML) and once with complete cases:

m1_fit      <- mediation$fiml[[1]]
m1_listwise <- mediation$listwise[[1]]

What does the model look like?

Step 6 · Latent blocks all persons
Does the result hold if measurement error is modelled? The composites treat each block as if it were measured without error. A structural-after-measurement model (SAM; Rosseel & Loh, 2024) first estimates how the scales measure each block and then the paths between the latent blocks; in its local form, misfit in one measurement model does not spread to the other blocks, as it would in a joint model. Each block is a latent factor measured by its scale scores, eight for H1, five for H2 and ten for H3, at both waves of the window. Scale scores rather than items keep the measurement models small (46 indicators instead of 200) and stay close to the composites, which average the same items. Within a block, each loading is equal at the two waves (over two adjacent waves, equal loadings cost the blocks almost no fit; Chapter 8), each scale’s residual covaries with itself over the waves, and the residuals of the scales made only of reverse-keyed items covary within a wave, for their shared wording (No Alienation and No Isolation in H1, the three non-frustration scales in H3; Chapter 5). The structural part is the model of Step 1, with its labels and effects.

Step 1 · The model all persons
What is regressed on what? Model 2 asks whether the first training still shows in September (T2), six months after it ended, measured from January (T0). The control group has not trained yet, so train_eg still compares trained with untrained persons. The composites at T2 are regressed as in Model 1, controlling for the composites at T0:

m2_model <- "
  # a: the training -> H1
  T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~ A*train_eg +
    T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # b1: H1 -> H2, b2: the training -> H2
  T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~ B1*T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness +
    B2*train_eg +
    T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # c1: H2 -> H3, c2: H1 -> H3, c3: the training -> H3
  T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing ~ C1*T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    C2*T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + C3*train_eg +
    T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the composites at T0 covary
  T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity
  T0_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  T0_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~~ T0_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the effects on H2
  indirectH2 := A*B1
  directH2   := B2
  totalH2    := B2 + A*B1
  # the effects on H3: via H1, via H2, via both in series
  ind_LET        := A*C2
  ind_CF         := B2*C1
  ind_serial     := A*B1*C1
  total_indirect := A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
  directH3       := C3
  totalH3        := C3 + A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
"

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model all persons
What is regressed on what? Model 3 starts after the first training, in March (T1), and asks whether the experimental group goes on changing until September (T2) without new training. Its controls, the composites at T1, already carry the training, so the model compares the groups in September given where they stood after the training; it is read with care.

m3_model <- "
  # a: the training -> H1
  T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~ A*train_eg +
    T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T1_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # b1: H1 -> H2, b2: the training -> H2
  T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~ B1*T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness +
    B2*train_eg +
    T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T1_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # c1: H2 -> H3, c2: H1 -> H3, c3: the training -> H3
  T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing ~ C1*T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    C2*T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + C3*train_eg +
    T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T1_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the composites at T1 covary
  T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity
  T1_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T1_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  T1_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~~ T1_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the effects on H2
  indirectH2 := A*B1
  directH2   := B2
  totalH2    := B2 + A*B1
  # the effects on H3: via H1, via H2, via both in series
  ind_LET        := A*C2
  ind_CF         := B2*C1
  ind_serial     := A*B1*C1
  total_indirect := A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
  directH3       := C3
  totalH3        := C3 + A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
"

Step 7 · What follows
What does the window show? No mediation between March and September: the total indirect effect does not carry, with the composites or with latent blocks. What remains of the training in this window points against it, through cognitive complexity, and rests on a model whose assumption does not hold at its start. The window goes into the comparison with the post hoc structure (Chapter 19) and into the table at the end of this chapter.

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model all persons
What is regressed on what? The control group trains between September (T2) and December (T3); train_cg marks the persons of its ten municipalities, and the experimental group, trained before, is now the comparison. The window replicates Model 1 with the roles of the groups reversed:

m4_model <- "
  # a: the training -> H1
  T3_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~ A*train_cg +
    T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # b1: H1 -> H2, b2: the training -> H2
  T3_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~ B1*T3_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness +
    B2*train_cg +
    T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # c1: H2 -> H3, c2: H1 -> H3, c3: the training -> H3
  T3_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing ~ C1*T3_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    C2*T3_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + C3*train_cg +
    T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness + T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity +
    T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the composites at T2 covary
  T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity
  T2_Hypothesis1_ListeningTogetherness ~~ T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  T2_Hypothesis2_CognitiveComplexity ~~ T2_Hypothesis3_Wellbeing
  # the effects on H2
  indirectH2 := A*B1
  directH2   := B2
  totalH2    := B2 + A*B1
  # the effects on H3: via H1, via H2, via both in series
  ind_LET        := A*C2
  ind_CF         := B2*C1
  ind_serial     := A*B1*C1
  total_indirect := A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
  directH3       := C3
  totalH3        := C3 + A*C2 + B2*C1 + A*B1*C1
"

        "cache/mediation.rds")

Chapter 13 leaves the models and turns to single persons: who improved, stayed the same or declined between two waves.

title: 11. Latent difference-in-differences
text:
11.1 How each construct is examined
Which constructs? The 20 constructs whose measurement Chapter 7 finds the same over the four waves and in both groups, each with the model Chapter 7 settled on: its adjustments of the stop rule and the items it freed. I Listen and Women Attitude stop in Chapter 7; their latent means are not compared here, and their scores enter the comparisons of means of Chapters 9 and 10.
What happens to each construct? Nine steps in four parts, always in the same order: the model, the effects, their robustness, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.





flowchart TB
  subgraph MODEL["the model"]
    direction LR
    S1["<b>Step 1</b><br>the model of Chapter 7<br>and what is added"] --> S2{{"<b>Step 2</b><br>the model of Chapter 7:<br>possible? as there?"}}
    S2 --> S3{{"<b>Step 3</b><br>covariates: possible?<br>only through the factors?"}}
  end
  subgraph EFFECTS["the effects"]
    direction LR
    S4["<b>Step 4</b><br>latent means"] --> S5["<b>Step 5</b><br>training effects:<br>DiD, d, replication"]
    S5 --> S6["<b>Step 6</b><br>drift of the<br>control group"]
  end
  subgraph ROBUST["robustness"]
    direction LR
    S7["<b>Step 7</b><br>restricted model"] --> S8["<b>Step 8</b><br>sample sets"]
  end
  V["<b>Step 9</b><br>what it shows"]
  MODEL --> EFFECTS
  EFFECTS --> ROBUST
  ROBUST --> V
  classDef both fill:#f0eaf8,stroke:#8e6bbf,color:#1d1d1f
  classDef verdict fill:#ffffff,stroke:#1d1d1f,color:#1d1d1f
  class S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6,S7,S8 both
  class V verdict
  style MODEL fill:#faf8fd,stroke:#8e6bbf
  style EFFECTS fill:#faf8fd,stroke:#8e6bbf
  style ROBUST fill:#faf8fd,stroke:#8e6bbf






Two rules hold along the way. At each check (the hexagons), a model that is not possible stops, as in Chapter 7. And what this chapter adds to the model of Chapter 7 is tested like a step there: if the covariates cost more fit than Chen’s cutoffs allow, the item they move most is freed; if that is not possible, the construct goes on without the covariates; its effects enter the tests like all others, marked as unadjusted.
How to read a construct below? It opens with its path through these steps, one row per step, and then takes them in the four parts, each under its own heading (also in the table of contents on the left). All steps use both groups at once; the label both groups or control beside each step names the data it looks at. Every step ends with what comes next.
The nine steps in detail:
The model:

The model. The final model of Chapter 7: one factor per wave, correlated over the waves; loadings and intercepts the same at every wave and in both groups (effects coding: the loadings average 1, the intercepts sum to 0, so a latent mean lies on the 0 to 10 scale of the answers); the residual covariances of Chapter 6 at every wave; each item’s residual linked to itself over the waves; the adjustments of the stop rule and the items freed for partial invariance, in the group where Chapter 7 needed them; and eight free latent means, one per group and wave. Each construct shows this model in full, part by part. This chapter adds two things:

Covariates. Age and sex, both centred on the whole sample, act on the factor of every wave, free in each group and at each wave. The latent means are then the means at the sample’s average age and share of women, and the difference-in-differences is adjusted for both. Persons without age or sex keep their answers (full information on the covariates, fiml.x).
Every contrast is a parameter. For each of the six windows between two waves: the change in the experimental group (EG), in the control group (CG), and their difference (DiD, positive when the experimental group gains more), with standard errors by the delta method.

The model of Chapter 7. Fitted again without the covariates, it goes through the checks of Chapter 7 (7.1, Step 3) and must reproduce Chapter 7: the same χ².
The covariates. The model with the covariates goes through the same checks. Then the one assumption the covariates add is tested: that age and sex act on the answers only through the factor. The comparison model gives each covariate a direct effect on every item at every wave instead; the model of Step 1 is nested in it. The step holds under Chen’s cutoffs (the CFI drops by no more than .010, the RMSEA rises by no more than .015), as the steps of Chapter 7. If it fails, the score test names the item and covariate that strain most, and that direct effect is freed at every wave, in both groups, until the step holds (as the partial invariance of Chapter 7). At least two items must keep their answers free of direct effects; where that is not possible, the construct goes on without the covariates. Next to the test, the fit with the covariates is set beside the fit of Chapter 7, for description: the two models do not hold the same variables, so their fit indices cannot be compared as a test.

The effects:

Latent means. The eight latent means with their 95 % confidence intervals, as a table and as a figure.
The training effects. The DiD of the two training windows: T0 to T1, when the experimental group trains (a positive DiD), and T2 to T3, when the control group trains (a negative DiD, since DiD is always experimental minus control); significant at p < .05. Their size is the latent d: the DiD divided by the latent standard deviation at T0, pooled over the two groups (Hancock, 2001), with Cohen’s (1988) labels: below .2 negligible, from .2 small, from .5 medium, from .8 large. Each window tests all 20 constructs at once, so their p-values are adjusted by Benjamini and Hochberg (1995), within each window (11.7). Last, the wait-list design adds a test: if the training works the same in both groups, the two effects cancel out, DiD (T0 to T1) + DiD (T2 to T3) = 0. A replication test near 0 supports this; it is a significance test, not an equivalence test.
Drift of the control group. Before its own training, the control group may change as well, through repeated answering, the season, or contact with colleagues who were trained: its change from T0 to T1, T0 to T2 and T1 to T2. The DiD of the first window subtracts exactly the change from T0 to T1.

Robustness:

The restricted model. The design suggests a sparer model: the control group keeps its January level until its own training (T0 = T1 = T2), and the experimental group keeps the level it reached after its own training (T1 = T2 = T3). These four equality constraints on the latent means are tested against the model of Step 3 by the scaled χ² difference (Satorra & Bentler, 2001); p < .05 rejects them.
The sample sets. The two training effects on the sample sets of Chapter 14, from S0 (all questionnaires, the model of Step 3) to S9; S7 equals S0. A set keeps some questionnaires of a person and drops the others, and the person enters the models with the waves the set keeps. Counted are the sets in which an effect is significant in the expected direction.

What follows:

What follows. What the construct shows: the two training effects side by side, read together with their correction for multiple testing and the sample sets of Step 8; then the model and the effects that go on to the synthesis of Chapter 20.

How are the checks and the cutoffs computed? As in Chapter 7:

# the two checks of every model, as in Chapter 7: converged, and a
# possible solution (lavaan's check for negative variances and covariances
# that are not positive definite); a model that cannot be estimated at all
# (NULL) is not possible
gates <- \(fit) {
  converged <- !is.null(fit) && lavInspect(fit, "converged")
  tibble(converged,
         admissible = converged &&
           isTRUE(suppressWarnings(lavInspect(fit, "post.check"))))
}

# Chen's (2007) cutoffs for more than 300 persons
holds_chen <- \(delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA) {
  delta_CFI >= -.010 & delta_RMSEA <= .015
}

title: 11. Latent difference-in-differences
text:
11.2 Data and tools
Which data? The wide data of Chapter 2, one row per person with the four waves side by side, with sex centred on the whole sample like age; and the results of the script that fits the restricted models and the models on the sample sets (Steps 7 and 8):

# sex as a covariate, centred like age_c (Chapter 2)
df_wide <- df_wide |>
  mutate(female_c = female - mean(female, na.rm = TRUE))

restricted  <- readRDS("cache/latent_did_restricted.rds") # Step 7
latent_sets <- readRDS("cache/latent_did_sets.rds")       # Step 8

# the p-values of the two training effects, corrected by Benjamini and
# Hochberg (1995) within each window over all 20 constructs; S0 of the
# sample sets is the model of Steps 4 to 6 (Step 8), so every construct can
# read its corrected p in Step 9, before 11.7 sets them side by side
corrected <- latent_sets |>
  filter(set == "S0") |>
  unnest(estimates) |>
  filter(label %in% c("DiD_T01", "DiD_T23")) |>
  mutate(p_BH = p.adjust(pvalue, method = "BH"), .by = label) |>
  select(construct, label, p_BH)

df_wide |>
  summarise(persons = n(), without_age = sum(is.na(age_c)),
            without_sex = sum(is.na(female)), .by = condition)

Which tools? The models of every step are fitted with their own call for each construct. One file writes their syntax from the model of Chapter 7; small functions build the tables and draw the figures. Fitting the restricted models and the models on the nine sample sets takes a while, so they run in a script of their own:

SyntaxScriptTablesFigures



# The latent difference-in-differences of Chapter 11: the final model of a
# construct from Chapter 7, in both groups over the four waves, with the
# covariates and the contrasts that Chapter 11 adds
#
# did_syntax() takes the status of a construct as Chapter 7 saved it
# (cache/invariance.rds, `adopted`): its adjustments of the stop rule
# (estimates set at 0, the autocorrelations) and the items freed for partial
# invariance. Loadings and intercepts are equal over the waves and the
# groups; the eight latent means are free (Chapter 7, Step 8).
#
# What Chapter 11 adds:
#   covariates  age and sex, both centred on the whole sample, regressed on
#               every factor, free in each group and at each wave; the
#               latent means are then the means at the sample's average age
#               and share of women
#   contrasts   for each of the six windows between two waves the change in
#               each group (EG, CG) and their difference (DiD, positive when
#               the experimental group gains more), and the wait-list
#               replication: the two training effects add up to 0
# Needs R/measurement.R, R/longitudinal_models.R and R/longitudinal_effects.R.

# the six windows between two waves
windows <- c(
  T01 = "T0 to T1, January to March: the experimental group trains",
  T02 = "T0 to T2, January to September: durability",
  T03 = "T0 to T3, January to December: the full year",
  T12 = "T1 to T2, March to September: maintenance",
  T13 = "T1 to T3, March to December: maintenance and control training",
  T23 = "T2 to T3, September to December: the control group trains"
)

# a window's name from its two waves: T0 and T1 -> T01
window_of <- \(pair) str_c("T", str_sub(pair[1], 2), str_sub(pair[2], 2))

# the final model of Chapter 7 for a construct
chapter7_syntax <- \(status) {
  invariance_syntax(status$construct, loadings = "groups",
                    intercepts = "groups",
                    zero = status$set_to_0[[1]], free = status$freed[[1]],
                    autocorrelations = status$autocorrelations[[1]])
}

# the lines Chapter 11 adds: the covariates on every factor
covariate_lines <- \(covariates = c("age_c", "female_c")) {
  str_c("F_", waves, " ~ ", str_c(covariates, collapse = " + "))
}

# the lines Chapter 11 adds: every contrast as a parameter
contrast_lines <- \() {
  change <- \(group, p) str_c("(m_", group, "_", p[2], " - m_", group, "_",
                              p[1], ")")
  per_window <- map(wave_pairs, \(p) c(
    str_c("EG_", window_of(p), " := ", change("exp", p)),
    str_c("CG_", window_of(p), " := ", change("con", p)),
    str_c("DiD_", window_of(p), " := ", change("exp", p), " - ",
          change("con", p))))
  replication <- str_c(
    "Replication_test := ",
    change("exp", c("T0", "T1")), " - ", change("con", c("T0", "T1")),
    " + ", change("exp", c("T2", "T3")), " - ", change("con", c("T2", "T3")))
  c(unlist(per_window), replication)
}

# direct effects of a covariate on an item at every wave, for the items
# whose answers age or sex move beyond the factor ("Flourishing3 age_c")
direct_lines <- \(direct) {
  map(direct, \(entry) {
    parts <- str_split_1(entry, " ")
    str_c(parts[1], "_", waves, " ~ ", parts[2])
  }) |>
    unlist()
}

# the model of Chapter 11: Chapter 7's model, with or without the
# covariates (and the direct effects the covariate step frees), and the
# contrasts
did_syntax <- \(status, covariates = TRUE, direct = character()) {
  c(chapter7_syntax(status),
    if (covariates) c(covariate_lines(), direct_lines(direct)),
    contrast_lines()) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# the comparison model of the covariate step: each covariate with a direct
# effect on every item at every wave and no path to the factors; the model
# with paths to the factors only is nested in it
direct_everywhere <- \(status) {
  items <- model_items[[status$construct]]
  c(chapter7_syntax(status),
    str_c(at(items, rep(waves, each = length(items))),
          " ~ age_c + female_c")) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# two groups, robust maximum likelihood; with the covariates, persons
# without age or sex keep their answers (missing = "fiml.x")
fit_did <- \(model, data = df_wide, covariates = TRUE) {
  sem(model, data = data, group = "condition", estimator = "MLR",
      missing = if (covariates) "fiml.x" else "fiml")
}




# Sensitivity of the latent difference-in-differences of Chapter 11: the
# restricted model with level means outside the training, and the models of
# the constructs that enter Chapter 11 on the sample sets S0 to S9. Each
# stage is saved as soon as it is done.
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapters 4 and 7:
#   Rscript scripts/latent_did_sensitivity.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
source("R/measurement.R")
source("R/longitudinal_models.R")
source("R/longitudinal_effects.R")
source("R/latent_did.R")
df         <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")         # one row per questionnaire
df_wide    <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds")    # one row per person
careless   <- readRDS("cache/careless.rds")   # flags S8, S9 (Chapter 4)
invariance <- readRDS("cache/invariance.rds") # the models of Chapter 7
item_names <- names(select(df, ListenOther1:CompetenceNonFrustrated4))

# sex centred on the whole sample, as in Chapter 11 (age_c is centred)
df_wide <- df_wide |>
  mutate(female_c = female - mean(female, na.rm = TRUE))

# the constructs that enter Chapter 11, with their status from Chapter 7
# and the covariate step of Chapter 11 (11.3: with or without the
# covariates, and the direct effects it frees)
entering <- invariance$adopted |>
  filter(chapter_11) |>
  left_join(readRDS("cache/latent_did_models.rds"), by = "construct")

# the model of Chapter 11 for a construct, and its fit
model_of <- \(status) did_syntax(status, covariates = status$covariates,
                                 direct = status$direct[[1]])
fit_of <- \(model, status, data = df_wide) {
  fit_did(model, data = data, covariates = status$covariates)
}

log_step <- \(...) cat(format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), ..., "\n")

# convergence and admissibility of a fit
checks <- \(fit) {
  tibble(converged  = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
         admissible = isTRUE(suppressWarnings(lavInspect(fit, "post.check"))))
}

# the estimates of all labelled parameters of a model (as in Chapter 11)
estimates <- \(fit) {
  parameterEstimates(fit) |>
    filter(label != "") |>
    distinct(label, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(label, est, se, z, pvalue) |>
    as_tibble()
}

# a fit index as a plain number
index <- \(fit, name) as.numeric(fitMeasures(fit, name))

# Stage 1: the restricted model. The control group keeps its level until
# its own training (T0 = T1 = T2), the experimental group keeps the level
# it reached after its own (T1 = T2 = T3): four constraints on the latent
# means, tested against the free model by the scaled χ² difference
# (Satorra & Bentler, 2001).
restricted_means <- c("m_con_T0 == m_con_T1", "m_con_T1 == m_con_T2",
                      "m_exp_T1 == m_exp_T2", "m_exp_T2 == m_exp_T3")

# the free and the restricted model of a construct and their comparison
restriction_test <- \(status) {
  log_step("restricted means:", status$construct)
  free       <- fit_of(model_of(status), status)
  restricted <- fit_of(str_c(c(model_of(status), restricted_means),
                             collapse = "\n"), status)
  test <- lavTestLRT(free, restricted, method = "satorra.bentler.2001")
  tibble(chisq_free       = index(free, "chisq.scaled"),
         df_free          = index(free, "df"),
         chisq_restricted = index(restricted, "chisq.scaled"),
         df_restricted    = index(restricted, "df"),
         delta_chisq      = test[2, "Chisq diff"],
         delta_df         = test[2, "Df diff"],
         p                = test[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"]) |>
    bind_cols(checks(restricted))
}

restricted <- entering |>
  mutate(test = map(seq_len(n()), \(i)
    suppressWarnings(restriction_test(entering[i, ])))) |>
  select(construct, test) |>
  unnest(test)
saveRDS(restricted, "cache/latent_did_restricted.rds")

# Stage 2: the sample sets of Chapter 14 (S7 equals S0, Chapter 1)
df <- df |>
  left_join(select(careless, id, Occasion, s8_no_careless,
                   s9_no_careless_strict),
            by = c("id", "Occasion"))

sample_sets <- tribble(
  ~set, ~flag,
  "S0", NA,
  "S1", "s1_complete",
  "S2", "s2_no_singletons",
  "S3", "s3_has_T0",
  "S4", "s4_T0_plus_post",
  "S5", "s5_group_baseline",
  "S6", "s6_no_T0_dropouts",
  "S8", "s8_no_careless",
  "S9", "s9_no_careless_strict"
)

# the wide data of a set: the questionnaires it keeps, side by side as in
# Chapter 2, with each person's covariates; persons without a questionnaire
# in the set drop out
set_wide <- \(flag) {
  kept <- if (is.na(flag)) df else filter(df, .data[[flag]])
  kept |>
    select(id, condition, Occasion, all_of(item_names)) |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols     = c(id, condition),
                names_from  = Occasion,
                values_from = all_of(item_names),
                names_glue  = "{.value}_{Occasion}") |>
    left_join(select(df_wide, id, age_c, female_c), by = "id")
}

# the model of a construct on the data of a set
set_model <- \(set, data, i) {
  status <- entering[i, ]
  log_step(set, status$construct)
  fit <- suppressWarnings(fit_of(model_of(status), status, data = data))
  checks(fit) |>
    mutate(control      = lavInspect(fit, "nobs")[1],
           experimental = lavInspect(fit, "nobs")[2],
           estimates    = list(estimates(fit)))
}

latent_sets <- sample_sets |>
  mutate(data = map(flag, set_wide)) |>
  cross_join(tibble(i = seq_len(nrow(entering)))) |>
  mutate(construct = entering$construct[i],
         model     = pmap(list(set, data, i), set_model)) |>
  select(set, construct, model) |>
  unnest(model)
saveRDS(latent_sets, "cache/latent_did_sets.rds")
log_step("done")




# ✓ or ✗ for a check or a step
mark <- \(x) if_else(x, "✓", "✗")

# the fit of a model in one row (ML indices, as in Chapter 7)
fit_row <- \(fit) {
  fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq.scaled", "df", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr")) |>
    as.list() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    rename(chisq = chisq.scaled, CFI = cfi, RMSEA = rmsea, SRMR = srmr)
}

# "p = .042", or "p < .001"
p_text <- \(p) if_else(p < .001, "p < .001", str_c("p = ", apa(p, 3)))

# Cohen's (1988) benchmarks for |d|
cohen <- \(d) cut(abs(d), breaks = c(0, .2, .5, .8, Inf), right = FALSE,
                  labels = c("negligible", "small", "medium", "large"))

# Step 9: the two training effects of a construct side by side, with what
# Steps 5 and 8 and the correction of 11.7 say about them: the DiD in
# points of the answer scale, its latent d and p, the p corrected for
# testing all 20 constructs in its window, and in how many of the nine
# sample sets it is significant in the expected direction, with the range
# of its estimate there
verdict_table <- \(construct, est, p, d, sets) {
  windows <- c(DiD_T01 = "T0–T1", DiD_T23 = "T2–T3")
  in_sets <- sets |>
    unnest(estimates) |>
    filter(label %in% names(windows)) |>
    summarise(significant = sum(pvalue < .05 &
                                  if_else(label == "DiD_T01", est > 0,
                                          est < 0)),
              n = n(), low = min(est), high = max(est), .by = label)
  tibble(label = names(windows), window = windows,
         DiD = est[label], d = d[label], p = p[label]) |>
    left_join(corrected |> filter(construct == .env$construct),
              by = "label") |>
    left_join(in_sets, by = "label") |>
    transmute(label, window, DiD, d, size = as.character(cohen(d)), p, p_BH,
              sets = str_c(significant, " of ", n),
              range = str_c(apa(low), " to ", apa(high)),
              significant)
}

# the table of verdict_table() as shown, rounded
show_verdict <- \(verdict) {
  verdict |>
    transmute(window, DiD = round(DiD, 2), d = round(d, 2), size,
              p = round(p, 3), `p corrected` = round(p_BH, 3),
              `sets with the effect` = sets, `range in sets` = range)
}

# a parameter of the longitudinal model in words: "item 1 at T2",
# "item 1, T2 with T3", "item 1 with item 2 at T0", "the factors at T0 and
# T1", "item 3 at T1 on the factor at T2"
in_words <- \(lhs, rhs = lhs, op = "~~") {
  item <- \(v) str_c("item ", str_extract(v, "[0-9]+(?=_T)"))
  wave <- \(v) str_extract(v, "T[0-3]$")
  case_when(
    op == "=~"            ~ str_c(item(rhs), " at ", wave(rhs),
                                  " on the factor at ", wave(lhs)),
    str_starts(lhs, "F_") & lhs == rhs ~ str_c("the factor at ", wave(lhs)),
    str_starts(lhs, "F_") ~ str_c("the factors at ", wave(lhs), " and ",
                                  wave(rhs)),
    lhs == rhs            ~ str_c(item(lhs), " at ", wave(lhs)),
    item(lhs) == item(rhs) ~ str_c(item(lhs), ", ", wave(lhs), " with ",
                                   wave(rhs)),
    .default = str_c(item(lhs), " with ", item(rhs), " at ", wave(lhs)))
}

# checks 1 to 6 of 7.1: did the estimation work, and is the solution
# proper? Each with what is looked at, its value and its criterion; in a
# model of two groups, the worst of both
proper_checks <- \(fit) {
  converged <- lavInspect(fit, "converged")
  labels    <- lavInspect(fit, "group.label")
  in_group  <- \(g) if (length(labels) > 1) str_c(" (", labels[g], ")") else ""
  # one group: no group column, so group 1
  with_group <- \(x) if (is.null(x$group)) mutate(x, group = 1) else x
  estimates  <- with_group(parameterEstimates(fit))
  std        <- with_group(standardizedSolution(fit))
  smallest  <- \(what) {
    matrices <- lavInspect(fit, what)
    if (is.matrix(matrices)) matrices <- list(matrices)
    min(map_dbl(matrices, \(m) min(eigen(m, symmetric = TRUE,
                                         only.values = TRUE)$values)))
  }
  variance <- estimates |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs, !str_starts(lhs, "F_")) |>
    slice_min(est, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  correlation <- std |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs) |>
    slice_max(abs(est.std), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  se <- parTable(fit) |> filter(free > 0) |> pull(se)
  # lavaan's own tolerance for an eigenvalue at 0
  above_0 <- \(x) x > -.Machine$double.eps^(3 / 4)
  tribble(
    ~check, ~what, ~value, ~criterion, ~holds,
    "1 estimation", "converged", if (converged) "yes" else "no", "yes",
    converged,
    "2 variances", str_c("smallest residual variance: ",
                         in_words(variance$lhs), in_group(variance$group)),
    apa(variance$est, 3), "above 0", above_0(variance$est),
    "3 correlations", str_c("largest correlation: ",
                            in_words(correlation$lhs, correlation$rhs),
                            in_group(correlation$group)),
    apa(correlation$est.std, 3), "within ±1",
    abs(correlation$est.std) <= 1,
    "4 residuals", "smallest eigenvalue of the residual covariances",
    apa(smallest("theta"), 3), "above 0", above_0(smallest("theta")),
    "5 factors", "smallest eigenvalue of the factor covariances",
    apa(smallest("cov.lv"), 3), "above 0", above_0(smallest("cov.lv")),
    "6 standard errors", "estimated for every free parameter",
    if (all(is.finite(se) & se > 0)) "yes" else "no", "yes",
    all(is.finite(se) & se > 0))
}

# checks 7 to 11 of 7.1: the overall fit (ML indices), where the model
# strains most, and its weakest loading. The CFI decides only for the
# configural model in all persons (`judge_fit`); the rest is reported
fit_checks <- \(fit, judge_fit = FALSE) {
  labels   <- lavInspect(fit, "group.label")
  in_group <- \(g) {
    if (length(labels) > 1) str_c(" (", labels[g], ")") else ""
  }
  fm <- fitMeasures(fit, c("cfi", "rmsea", "rmsea.ci.lower",
                           "rmsea.ci.upper", "srmr"))
  strain <- suppressWarnings(modindices(fit, sort. = TRUE,
                                        maximum.number = 1))
  loading <- standardizedSolution(fit) |>
    filter(op == "=~") |>
    slice_min(est.std, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  tribble(
    ~check, ~what, ~value, ~criterion, ~holds,
    "7 fit", "CFI", apa(fm["cfi"], 3),
    if (judge_fit) "at least .90" else "reported",
    if (judge_fit) fm[["cfi"]] >= .90 else NA,
    "8 fit", "RMSEA [90 % interval]",
    str_c(apa(fm["rmsea"], 3), " [", apa(fm["rmsea.ci.lower"], 3), ", ",
          apa(fm["rmsea.ci.upper"], 3), "]"), "reported", NA,
    "9 fit", "SRMR", apa(fm["srmr"], 3), "reported", NA,
    "10 strain", str_c("largest modification index: ",
                       in_words(strain$lhs, strain$rhs, strain$op),
                       in_group(strain$group %||% 1)),
    sprintf("%.1f", strain$mi), "reported", NA,
    "11 estimates", str_c("smallest standardized loading: ",
                          in_words(loading$rhs),
                          in_group(loading$group %||% 1)),
    apa(loading$est.std, 2), "reported", NA)
}

# all eleven checks of a model, ✓ or ✗ where a check decides
model_checks <- \(fit, judge_fit = FALSE) {
  bind_rows(proper_checks(fit), fit_checks(fit, judge_fit)) |>
    mutate(holds = if_else(is.na(holds), "–", mark(holds)))
}

# checks 1 to 6 of every model of a step, side by side: is each possible?
possible_table <- \(fits) {
  fits |>
    map(\(fit) proper_checks(fit) |>
          transmute(check = str_remove(check, "^[0-9]+ "),
                    holds = mark(holds))) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "model") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = check, values_from = holds)
}

# the checks a model fails, in words: "Check 3 (largest correlation: item
# 1, T2 with T3, -1.007) and check 4 (...) fail"
failed_checks <- \(checks) {
  failing <- checks |> filter(holds == "✗")
  failing |>
    transmute(text = str_c("check ", str_extract(check, "^[0-9]+"), " (",
                           what, ", ", value, ")")) |>
    pull(text) |>
    str_flatten_comma(", and ") |>
    str_replace("^c", "C") |>
    str_c(if (nrow(failing) == 1) " fails" else " fail")
}

# the standardized loading of every item at every wave
loading_table <- \(fit) {
  standardizedSolution(fit) |>
    filter(op == "=~") |>
    transmute(item    = str_c("item ", str_extract(rhs, "[0-9]+(?=_T)")),
              wave    = str_remove(lhs, "^F_"),
              loading = round(est.std, 2)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = wave, values_from = loading)
}

# the correlation of the factors at every pair of waves
factor_correlations <- \(fit) {
  standardizedSolution(fit) |>
    filter(op == "~~", str_starts(lhs, "F_"), lhs != rhs) |>
    transmute(waves = str_c(str_remove(lhs, "^F_"), "–",
                            str_remove(rhs, "^F_")),
              r     = round(est.std, 2)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = waves, values_from = r)
}

# what checks 1 to 6 of a model say, in one sentence
proper_sentence <- \(checks) {
  if (all(checks$holds[1:6] == "✓")) {
    return("Checks 1 to 6 hold: the solution is proper.")
  }
  str_c(failed_checks(checks), ": the solution is not possible.")
}

# the lines of the model syntax an adjustment changes, all of them: "-"
# before, "+" after
syntax_changes <- \(before, after) {
  before <- str_split_1(before, "\n")
  after  <- str_split_1(after, "\n")
  cat(str_c("- ", setdiff(before, after)), str_c("+ ", setdiff(after, before)),
      sep = "\n")
}

# the complete model as lavaan reads it, every line once and in its order,
# each part under its heading: first the final model of Chapter 7, then what
# this chapter adds; with `added_only = TRUE`, the added parts alone
show_model <- \(model, added_only = FALSE) {
  # one entry per statement: a factor stays together with its items
  lines <- str_split_1(model, "\n(?!  )")
  two_items <- !any(str_detect(lines, "NA\\*"))
  headings <- c(
    loadings   = if (two_items) "one factor per wave; both items load 1" else
      "one factor per wave; NA* frees the first loading",
    coding     = "effects coding: the loadings average 1, the intercepts
                  sum to 0",
    means      = "the latent means, free in each group",
    intercepts = "the intercepts",
    factors    = "the factors correlate over the waves",
    pairs      = "the residual covariances of Chapter 6, at every wave",
    itself     = "each item's residual with itself over the waves",
    equal      = "each residual variance equal in both groups
                  (adjustment C)",
    zero       = "set at 0 in one group (adjustment A)",
    covariates = "age and sex on the factor of every wave",
    direct     = "age or sex directly on single items",
    contrasts  = "every contrast as a parameter") |>
    str_squish()
  added <- c("covariates", "direct", "contrasts")

  # the part of each line, from its operator and what it links
  stem <- \(x) str_remove(x, "_T\\d$")
  lhs  <- str_extract(lines, "^\\S+")
  rhs  <- str_extract(lines, "[^ *]+$")
  covariate <- str_detect(lines, " ~ (age_c|female_c)")
  part <- case_when(
    str_detect(lines, " =~ ")                     ~ "loadings",
    str_detect(lines, " == ")                     ~ "coding",
    str_detect(lines, " := ")                     ~ "contrasts",
    covariate & str_starts(lines, "F_")           ~ "covariates",
    covariate                                     ~ "direct",
    str_detect(lines, " ~ ") & str_starts(lines, "F_") ~ "means",
    str_detect(lines, " ~ ")                      ~ "intercepts",
    str_detect(lines, "c\\(0, NA\\)|c\\(NA, 0\\)") ~ "zero",
    str_starts(lines, "F_")                       ~ "factors",
    str_detect(lines, " ~~ v\\d")               ~ "equal",
    stem(lhs) == stem(rhs)                        ~ "itself",
    .default = "pairs")

  tibble(part, line = lines) |>
    filter(!added_only | part %in% added) |>
    mutate(run    = consecutive_id(part),
           source = if_else(part %in% added, "added here", "Chapter 7")) |>
    summarise(text = str_c("# ", first(source), ": ", headings[first(part)],
                           "\n", str_flatten(line, "\n")),
              .by = run) |>
    pull(text) |>
    str_flatten("\n\n") |>
    cat("\n", sep = "")
}

# the covariate step: the model with the covariates on the factors only,
# against the comparison model with their direct effects on every item;
# what the restriction costs, Chen's cutoffs, and the scaled χ² difference
covariate_step <- \(nested, comparison) {
  list(`direct effects on every item` = comparison,
       `only through the factors`     = nested) |>
    map(fit_row) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "model") |>
    mutate(delta_CFI   = CFI - lag(CFI),
           delta_RMSEA = RMSEA - lag(RMSEA),
           p = c(NA, lavTestLRT(nested, comparison,
                                method = "satorra.bentler.2001")[
                                  2, "Pr(>Chisq)"]),
           Chen = holds_chen(delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA))
}

# the covariate step for the page
show_step <- \(step) {
  step |>
    transmute(model, df, CFI, RMSEA, ΔCFI = delta_CFI,
              ΔRMSEA = delta_RMSEA, p, Chen = mark(Chen)) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
}

# the score test of each direct effect of a covariate on an item, at every
# wave and in both groups, summed per item and covariate: how much the fit
# would gain if age or sex moved that item beyond the factor
score_direct <- \(fit, construct, freed = character()) {
  candidates <- expand_grid(item      = model_items[[construct]],
                            covariate = c("age_c", "female_c")) |>
    filter(!str_c(item, " ", covariate) %in% freed) |>
    mutate(parameter = map2(item, covariate, \(i, c)
      str_c(i, "_", waves, " ~ ", c))) |>
    unnest(parameter)
  suppressWarnings(lavTestScore(fit, add = candidates$parameter))$uni |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(item      = str_extract(lhs, "^[A-Za-z]+[0-9]+"),
           covariate = str_extract(lhs, "age_c|female_c")) |>
    summarise(X2 = sum(X2), .by = c(item, covariate)) |>
    arrange(desc(X2))
}

# defined parameters (the contrasts) of a model
contrasts_of <- \(fit, labels) {
  parameterEstimates(fit) |>
    filter(op == ":=", label %in% labels) |>
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = labels)) |>
    arrange(label) |>
    select(label, est, se, pvalue, ci.lower, ci.upper)
}

# the latent standard deviation at T0, pooled over the two groups
pooled_sd_T0 <- \(fit) {
  lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv") |>
    map_dbl(\(group) group["F_T0", "F_T0"]) |>
    mean() |>
    sqrt()
}




# the longitudinal model as a figure: one factor per wave (circles), its
# items below (boxes, by number), the loadings as arrows; above the factors
# their correlations, below the items each item's link to itself at the
# next wave (dashed: the residual covariances within a wave). The links
# between waves further apart are part of the model but not drawn.
# Estimates in `flagged` ("lhs ~~ rhs", from a fit) are drawn in red with
# their value; estimates in `fixed` (set at 0 by the stop rule) in green
plot_model <- \(construct, fit = NULL, flagged = character(),
                fixed = character()) {
  items <- model_items[[construct]]
  k     <- length(items)
  width <- k + 1.4                                  # the room of one wave
  box   <- tibble(wave = rep(waves, each = k), j = rep(seq_len(k), 4)) |>
    mutate(x        = (match(wave, waves) - 1) * width + j - 1,
           variable = str_c(items[j], "_", wave),
           key      = str_c(variable, " ~~ ", variable),
           mark     = case_when(key %in% flagged ~ "flagged",
                                key %in% fixed   ~ "fixed",
                                .default         = "none"))
  factor <- box |>
    summarise(x = mean(x), .by = wave)
  position <- \(v) box$x[match(v, box$variable)]
  pairs  <- residual_pairs |> filter(construct == .env$construct)
  within <- expand_grid(p = seq_len(nrow(pairs)), wave = waves) |>
    transmute(lhs = str_c(pairs$item_a[p], "_", wave),
              rhs = str_c(pairs$item_b[p], "_", wave))
  over_time <- expand_grid(j = seq_len(k), w = 1:3) |>
    transmute(lhs = str_c(items[j], "_", waves[w]),
              rhs = str_c(items[j], "_", waves[w + 1]))
  arcs <- \(links) mutate(links, x = position(lhs), xend = position(rhs),
                           span = round((xend - x) / width))
  # a flagged estimate with its value (a correlation as r, a variance as
  # estimated), a fixed one as 0
  value_of <- \(lhs, rhs) {
    if (is.null(fit)) return(rep("", length(lhs)))
    std <- standardizedSolution(fit)
    raw <- parameterEstimates(fit)
    at  <- \(tab) match(str_c(lhs, rhs), str_c(tab$lhs, tab$rhs))
    if_else(lhs == rhs, apa(raw$est[at(raw)], 3), apa(std$est.std[at(std)], 2))
  }
  marked <- bind_rows(flagged = tibble(key = flagged),
                      fixed   = tibble(key = fixed), .id = "mark") |>
    separate_wider_delim(key, " ~~ ", names = c("lhs", "rhs"),
                         cols_remove = FALSE) |>
    filter(lhs != rhs) |>
    arcs() |>
    mutate(text = if_else(mark == "fixed", "0", value_of(lhs, rhs)))
  colours <- c(none = "grey35", flagged = "#e34948", fixed = "#1baf7a")
  ggplot() +
    # the factor correlations: neighbouring waves, then two and three apart
    map(1:3, \(span) geom_curve(
      data = tibble(x = factor$x[1:(4 - span)],
                    xend = factor$x[(1 + span):4]),
      aes(x = x, y = 3.42, xend = xend, yend = 3.42),
      curvature = -.32 / span, colour = "grey62", linewidth = .35)) +
    geom_curve(data = arcs(over_time), aes(x = x, y = .62, xend = xend,
                                           yend = .62),
               curvature = .3, colour = "grey70", linewidth = .35) +
    geom_curve(data = arcs(within), aes(x = x, y = .62, xend = xend,
                                        yend = .62),
               curvature = .6, colour = "grey35", linewidth = .35,
               linetype = "dashed") +
    # the marked links: as deep as a link to the next wave, however far
    map(1:3, \(s) geom_curve(data = filter(marked, span == s),
                             aes(x = x, y = .62, xend = xend, yend = .62,
                                 colour = mark, linetype = mark),
                             curvature = .3 / s, linewidth = 1.1)) +
    geom_label(data = marked, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = .18, label = text,
                                  colour = mark),
               fill = "white", size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", linewidth = 0) +
    geom_segment(data = left_join(box, rename(factor, fx = x), by = "wave"),
                 aes(x = fx, y = 2.62, xend = x, yend = 1.33),
                 colour = "grey35", linewidth = .4,
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_tile(data = box, aes(x = x, y = 1, colour = mark), fill = "white",
              width = .76, height = .62, linewidth = .6) +
    geom_text(data = box, aes(x = x, y = 1,
                              label = str_remove(items[j], construct)),
              size = 3.8) +
    geom_label(data = filter(box, mark != "none") |>
                 mutate(text = if_else(mark == "fixed", "0",
                                       value_of(variable, variable))),
               aes(x = x, y = .18, label = text, colour = mark),
               fill = "white", size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", linewidth = 0) +
    geom_point(data = factor, aes(x = x, y = 3), shape = 21, size = 16,
               fill = "#f0efec", colour = "grey35") +
    geom_text(data = factor, aes(x = x, y = 3, label = wave), size = 4,
              fontface = "bold") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(flagged = "solid", fixed = "dashed"),
                          guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-.05, 4.15), clip = "off") +
    theme_void(base_size = 11)
}
# the latent means of the two groups at the four waves, with their 95 %
# confidence intervals; shaded: the training of the experimental group
# (orange) and of the control group (blue)
plot_latent_means <- \(fit) {
  parameterEstimates(fit) |>
    filter(op == "~1", str_starts(lhs, "F_")) |>
    mutate(group = if_else(str_starts(label, "m_con"), "Control",
                           "Experimental"),
           wave  = str_remove(lhs, "^F_")) |>
    ggplot(aes(wave, est, colour = group, group = group)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = str_c(waves, "\n", months_list)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 1, xmax = 2, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#eb6834", alpha = .08) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 3, xmax = 4, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .08) +
    geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = .2), linewidth = .7) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ci.lower, ymax = ci.upper),
                    position = position_dodge(width = .2), size = .35) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Control = "#2a78d6",
                                   Experimental = "#eb6834")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "latent mean (0 to 10)", colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

# the two training effects with their 95 % intervals against 0 (dashed);
# filled: significant at p < .05
plot_did <- \(fit) {
  contrasts_of(fit, c("DiD_T01", "DiD_T23")) |>
    mutate(window = if_else(label == "DiD_T01",
                            "T0 to T1: the experimental group trains",
                            "T2 to T3: the control group trains"),
           window = fct_rev(factor(window)),
           significant = pvalue < .05) |>
    ggplot(aes(est, window, colour = window)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ci.lower, xmax = ci.upper), width = .2) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = significant), size = 3.4, fill = "white") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21),
                       guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "T0 to T1: the experimental group trains" = "#eb6834",
      "T2 to T3: the control group trains"      = "#2a78d6"),
      guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "DiD, experimental minus control (0 to 10 scale)", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

# the two training effects on every sample set (Chapter 14) with their
# 95 % intervals; S0 is the model of this chapter; filled: significant
plot_sets <- \(sets) {
  sets |>
    unnest(estimates) |>
    filter(label %in% c("DiD_T01", "DiD_T23")) |>
    mutate(window = if_else(label == "DiD_T01", "T0 to T1", "T2 to T3"),
           set    = fct_rev(factor(set)),
           significant = pvalue < .05) |>
    ggplot(aes(est, set, colour = window)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = est - 1.96 * se, xmax = est + 1.96 * se),
                  width = .25) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = significant), size = 2.6, fill = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~ window, nrow = 1) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21),
                       guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("T0 to T1" = "#eb6834",
                                   "T2 to T3" = "#2a78d6"),
                        guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "DiD with its 95 % interval", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

Which model does Chapter 7 hand on? Its status there: the estimates the stop rule set at 0, the items freed, and the autocorrelations:

lo_status <- invariance$adopted |>
  filter(construct == "ListenOther")

lo_status |>
  transmute(status, set_to_0 = map_chr(set_to_0, \(x) str_flatten(x, "; ")),

title: 15. Item pruning
text:
15.1 How each rule is examined
What happens to each rule? The same five steps, in the same order and in three parts: the rule, its evidence, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.





flowchart TB
  subgraph P0["the rule"]
    direction LR
    S1["<b>Step 1</b><br>the starting point"]
    S1 --> S2["<b>Step 2</b><br>the rule"]
  end
  subgraph P1["the evidence: January"]
    direction LR
    S3["<b>Step 3</b><br>the evidence"]
    S3 --> S4{{"<b>Step 4</b><br>the result"}}
  end
  V["<b>Step 5</b><br>what follows"]
  P0 --> P1
  P1 --> V
  classDef all fill:#efeff2,stroke:#8a8a8a,color:#1d1d1f
  classDef verdict fill:#ffffff,stroke:#1d1d1f,color:#1d1d1f
  class S1,S2,S3,S4 all
  class V verdict
  style P0 fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a
  style P1 fill:#fafafa,stroke:#8a8a8a






The five steps in detail:
The rule:

The starting point. The items the rule looks at, in their wording where it matters, and how many items are still in the pool when the rule applies.
The rule. When an item leaves the pool, and why. The rules apply in a fixed order: ceiling, negative wording, the women’s attitude block. An item that meets more than one rule leaves under the first.

The evidence:

The evidence. The numbers on which the rule decides, item by item, in the T0 questionnaires: for the ceiling, the mean of each item, which must not lie above 9.7 on the scale from 0 to 10; for negative wording, how strongly each item moves while the experimental group trains (a difference-in-differences d from T0 to T1), compared between the positively and the negatively worded items; for the women’s attitude block, how the answers spread over the scale.
The result. Which items leave, and how many stay in the pool.

What follows:

What follows. What the decision means for the scales, and where the remaining items go next.

title: 15. Item pruning
text:
15.2 Data and tools
Which data? The T0 questionnaires of both groups decide every rule: everyone answered them before the first training, so no training effect can shape the structure. The evidence on negative wording adds T1, the end of the first training window:

Next → Step 2, the rule: When does an item leave?


Step 2 · The rule January
When does an item leave? Every negatively worded item leaves. In a network, negatively worded items tend to form communities of their own, defined by the direction of the wording rather than by its content, and they invite more answering errors. The factor models of Chapter 6 show the pattern: the reverse-keyed items 7 to 9 of Rogerian Schema hardly correlate with items 1 to 6. If these items also carried the training effect, however, dropping them would cost signal. Step 3 therefore asks how much each item moves while the experimental group trains.
Next → Step 3, the evidence: How is the movement of an item measured?



The evidence · Steps 3 and 4

Step 3 · The evidence both groups
How is the movement of an item measured? By a difference-in-differences d per item: the change of each group’s mean from T0 to T1, divided by the standard deviation at T0 pooled over both groups, experimental minus control. Unlike the Δd of Chapter 9, the means use every questionnaire of a group and wave, not only persons who answered at both waves. The negatively worded items enter reverse-keyed, so a positive d always means a move toward the desired pole. First the mean, the variance and the number of answers per item, group and wave, here for one item:

title: 15. Item pruning
text:
15.4 All rules at a glance
What does each rule take out, and what remains of each scale? Each item with the first rule that applies to it:

reasons <- tibble(item = item_names) |>
  mutate(reason = case_when(
    item %in% ceil_items ~ "ceiling",
    item %in% neg_items  ~ "negative wording",
    item %in% wa_items   ~ "women's attitude block",
    .default = NA
  ))

pool <- reasons |>
  filter(is.na(reason)) |>
